        notations.each { dependencies.add(configuration, it) }
    }
}
def cucumberVersion = setting('cucumber.version', '7.23.0')
// The gates read Cucumber's message stream (acceptanceCheck, gherkinMutation). Cucumber 7 writes it with a JSON library
// of its own; Cucumber 8 needs Jackson 2 or 3 on the classpath and fails the run without it. jackson-databind goes in
// without a version, so a BOM or the Spring dependency-management plugin gives it the version it gives jackson-core and
// jackson-annotations (a databind of its own version next to Boot's jackson-core broke Cucumber at start); only where
// nothing names a version does jackson.version decide, as a version the kit prefers.
def jacksonForCucumber = (cucumberVersion.find(/^\d+/) ?: '0').toInteger() >= 8 &&
        configurations.getByName('acceptanceTestImplementation').dependencies.isEmpty()
addDefault('acceptanceTestImplementation', [
        dependencies.platform("io.cucumber:cucumber-bom:${cucumberVersion}"),
        'io.cucumber:cucumber-java',
        'io.cucumber:cucumber-junit-platform-engine'] +
        (setting('acceptance.spring', 'true').toBoolean() ? ['io.cucumber:cucumber-spring'] : []) +
        (jacksonForCucumber ? ['tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind'] : []))
if (jacksonForCucumber) {
    dependencies.constraints.add('acceptanceTestImplementation', 'tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind') {
        version { prefer setting('jackson.version', '3.2.1') }
    }
}
addDefault('archTestImplementation', ["com.tngtech.archunit:archunit:${setting('archunit.version', '1.5.1')}"])
addDefault('gauntletCheckstyle', ["com.puppycrawl.tools:checkstyle:${setting('checkstyle.version', '12.3.1')}"])
addDefault('gauntletCpd', ["net.sourceforge.pmd:pmd-cli:${setting('pmd.version', '7.27.0')}",     // pmdGate and cpdReport
                           "net.sourceforge.pmd:pmd-java:${setting('pmd.version', '7.27.0')}"])

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ cheap checks first

tasks.register('gauntletInfo') {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Prints which gauntlet files and settings this build uses.'
    def lines = [
            "gauntlet dir : ${gauntletDir}",
            "module       : ${moduleName ?: '(build at the repository root)'}",
            "properties   : config/gauntlet.properties" + ((moduleProperties != null && moduleProperties.exists()) ?
                    " + config/${moduleName}/gauntlet.properties (overlay)" : ''),
            "architecture : ${gauntletDir.toPath().relativize(configFile('architecture.properties').toPath())}",
            "checkstyle   : ${gauntletDir.toPath().relativize(configFile('checkstyle.xml').toPath())}",
            "pmd          : ${gauntletDir.toPath().relativize(configFile('pmd-ruleset.xml').toPath())}",
            "allowlists   : ${gauntletDir.toPath().relativize(configFile('integrity-allowlist.txt').toPath())}, " +
                    "${gauntletDir.toPath().relativize(configFile('crap-allowlist.txt').toPath())}, " +
                    "${gauntletDir.toPath().relativize(configFile('pit-runerror-allowlist.txt').toPath())}",
            "basePackage  : ${basePackage ?: '(not set)'}    glue: ${glue ?: '(not set)'}",
            "cucumber     : ${setting('cucumber.version', '7.23.0')}    scope: ${scope}    baseRef: ${baseRef}",
            "features     : ${featuresPath}",
            "tools        : PIT ${setting('pit.version', '1.22.1')}, ArchUnit ${setting('archunit.version', '1.5.1')}, " +
                    "Checkstyle ${setting('checkstyle.version', '12.3.1')}, PMD ${setting('pmd.version', '7.27.0')}, " +
                    "JaCoCo ${setting('jacoco.version', '0.8.15')}",
            "gate JVM    : version=${gateJavaVersion ?: '(Gradle JVM)'}; home=${gateJavaHome ?: '(from toolchain)'}"]
            .collect { it.toString() }
    gauntletConfig.stringPropertyNames().findAll { it.startsWith('project.') }.sort().each { key ->
        lines.add("${key} = ${gauntletConfig.getProperty(key)}".toString())
    }
    doLast {
        lines.each { println it }
        println "gate executable: ${gateJavaBin()}"
    }
}

tasks.register('gauntletScope') {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Prints the scope of the scoped checks; fails when scope=changed cannot tell what changed.'
    doLast {
        def problem = scopeProblem()
        if (problem == gitMissing) {
            throw new GradleException("gauntlet: ${problem} (no `git` could be started in ${projectDir}), so the changed " +
                    "files are unknown. Put git on the PATH of this build - a running Gradle daemon keeps the PATH it was " +
                    "started with - or run with -Pgauntlet.scope=all.")
        }
        if (problem) {
            def branch = baseRef.contains('/') ? baseRef.substring(baseRef.indexOf('/') + 1) : baseRef
            throw new GradleException("gauntlet: ${problem}, so the changed files are unknown. Fetch the base branch: " +
                    "git fetch origin +refs/heads/${branch}:refs/remotes/origin/${branch} (a single-branch clone needs the " +
                    "refspec; a shallow clone needs git fetch --unshallow origin first; CI needs full history: " +
                    "GIT_DEPTH=0 / fetch-depth: 0). Or set baseRef in gauntlet/config/gauntlet.properties, or run " +
                    "with -Pgauntlet.scope=all.")
        }
        def unreadable = (changedSources() ?: []).findAll { it.unreadable }*.path
        if (unreadable) {
            throw new GradleException("gauntlet: cannot read ${unreadable.join(', ')} as ${sourceEncoding()}, so the types the " +
                    "changed sources declare are unknown. Declare the real source encoding where javac takes it from: " +
                    "JavaCompile options.encoding (or -encoding in options.compilerArgs).")
        }
        logger.lifecycle('gauntlet scope: ' + (scope == 'all' ? 'whole codebase' :
                "changed vs ${baseRef} (merge-base ${mergeBase().take(10)}): ${changedFiles().size()} file(s)"))
    }
}

tasks.register('integrityCheck', Exec) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Finds disabled tests, coverage/mutation evasion, inline suppressions and gate tampering.'
    executable javaBin
    args sourceUtf8, "${tools}/IntegrityCheck.java", '--root', projectDir.absolutePath, '--features', featuresPath,
            '--allowlist', configFile('integrity-allowlist.txt').absolutePath
    doFirst {
        // every source tree with the charset of the task that compiles it: a UTF-16 test tree read as UTF-8
        // would hide @Disabled
        args '--encoding', sourceEncoding(),
                '--test-encoding', compileEncoding('compileTestJava') ?: sourceEncoding(),
                '--acceptance-encoding', compileEncoding('compileAcceptanceTestJava') ?: sourceEncoding()
    }
}

// Checkstyle runs through its CLI on purpose: the Gradle checkstyle plugin would hook into `check`/`build`
// and collide with a project's own Checkstyle setup.
tasks.register('checkstyleGate', JavaExec) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Size and structure rules from gauntlet/config/checkstyle.xml (main sources in scope).'
    dependsOn 'gauntletScope'
    mustRunAfter 'integrityCheck'
    classpath = configurations.gauntletCheckstyle
    mainClass = 'com.puppycrawl.tools.checkstyle.Main'
    systemProperty 'config_loc', configFile('checkstyle.xml').parentFile.absolutePath
    // Checkstyle cannot parse a module descriptor (Gradle's own checkstyle plugin leaves module-info.java out for
    // that reason), and stops with "found 0" when nothing is left to look at.
    def descriptor = 'module-info.java'
    def targets = { ->
        scanTargets().findAll { target ->
            target.isFile() ? target.name != descriptor : Files.walk(target.toPath()).withCloseable { paths ->
                paths.anyMatch { Files.isRegularFile(it) && it.fileName.toString() != descriptor }
            }
        }
    }
    def report = buildDirFile('reports/checkstyle/gauntlet.xml')
    args '-c', configFile('checkstyle.xml').absolutePath, '-f', 'xml', '-o', report.absolutePath,
            '-x', '[/\\\\]' + Pattern.quote(descriptor) + '$'
    // The CLI exits with the violation count, which the OS truncates to 8 bits (256 violations = exit 0),
    // so the verdict comes from the XML report instead.
    ignoreExitValue = true
    def complaints = new ByteArrayOutputStream()     // stderr: where Checkstyle names a file it could not parse
    errorOutput = complaints
    onlyIf { task -> !targets().isEmpty() || skippedByTheKit(task, 'no Java source in scope') }
    doFirst {
        args targets()*.absolutePath
        complaints.reset()
        report.delete()
        report.parentFile.mkdirs()
    }
    doLast {
        def said = complaints.toString()
        if (said.trim()) {
            System.err.println(said.trim())
        }
        // One file Checkstyle cannot parse stops the whole run and leaves the report cut off.
        def stopped = said =~ /(?m)^\S*CheckstyleException: Exception was thrown while processing (.+)$/
        if (stopped.find()) {
            def causes = said.readLines().findAll { it ==~ /Caused by: \S+: .+/ }
            throw new GradleException("Checkstyle could not analyse ${relativePath(stopped.group(1))}" +
                    (causes ? " (${causes.last().replaceFirst(/^Caused by: \S+: /, '')})" : '') + " and stopped there, so no " +
                    "file is judged. Fix the file if it does not compile; if it does, Checkstyle " +
                    "${setting('checkstyle.version', '12.3.1')} cannot read it (checkstyle.version in " +
                    "gauntlet/config/gauntlet.properties).")
        }
        if (!report.exists()) {
            throw new GradleException("Checkstyle did not produce ${report} - see the output above")
        }
        def files
        try {
            files = new groovy.xml.XmlSlurper().parse(report).file
        } catch (org.xml.sax.SAXException ignored) {
            throw new GradleException("Checkstyle did not finish ${report} - see the output above")
        }
        def violations = []
        files.each { f ->
            f.error.each { e ->
                def check = e.@source.toString().tokenize('.').last().replaceAll(/Check$/, '')
                violations << "[ERROR] ${f.@name}:${e.@line}: ${e.@message} [${check}]"
            }
        }
        violations.each { println it }
        if (violations) {
            throw new GradleException("Checkstyle: ${violations.size()} violation(s) of gauntlet/config/checkstyle.xml")
        }
        println 'Checkstyle: OK'
    }
}

// PMD through the same CLI as CPD, for the same reason as Checkstyle. It needs the compiled classes and their
// dependencies (--aux-classpath) so that rules about types, overrides and resources can resolve symbols.
// Suppressed violations (NOPMD, @SuppressWarnings("PMD...")) count as violations: rules are switched off
// only by the human, in gauntlet/config/pmd-ruleset.xml. Suppressions declared there (rule properties
// violationSuppressXPath and violationSuppressRegex, report types "xpath" and "regex") are that human decision and
// do not count.
tasks.register('pmdGate', JavaExec) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Anti-pattern rules from gauntlet/config/pmd-ruleset.xml (main sources in scope).'
    dependsOn 'gauntletScope', 'classes'
    mustRunAfter 'checkstyleGate'
    classpath = configurations.gauntletCpd
    mainClass = 'net.sourceforge.pmd.cli.PmdCli'
    def report = buildDirFile('reports/pmd/gauntlet.xml')
    args 'check', '--format', 'xml', '--report-file', report.absolutePath,
            '--no-fail-on-violation', '--no-cache', '--no-progress', '--show-suppressed'
    ignoreExitValue = true   // the verdict comes from the XML report, like checkstyleGate
    onlyIf { task -> !scanTargets().isEmpty() || skippedByTheKit(task, 'no Java source in scope') }
    doFirst {
        // PMD splits every value of --rulesets, --dir and --relativize-paths-with at commas: under "/home/me/Acme, Inc"
        // it loaded no rules, and a changed "Ledger,Copy.java" left it no file - "PMD: OK" on nothing. The ruleset and
        // the sources go relative to the directory PMD starts in (the report then names the sources that way too),
        // the sources as positional parameters after "--", which PMD takes whole.
        args(['--rulesets', relativeTo(workingDir, configFile('pmd-ruleset.xml')),
              '--use-version', "java-${java.targetCompatibility.majorVersion}".toString(), '--encoding', sourceEncoding()])
        // the JDK's own classes (jrt-fs.jar of the JDK running PMD) explicitly, or PMD warns about guessing them
        def jdk = javaLauncher.get().metadata.installationPath.asFile
        args '--aux-classpath', (sourceSets.main.compileClasspath + sourceSets.main.output.classesDirs +
                files(new File(jdk, 'lib/jrt-fs.jar'))).asPath
        args(['--'] + scanTargets().collect { relativeTo(workingDir, it) })
        report.delete()
        report.parentFile.mkdirs()
    }
    doLast {
        if (!report.exists()) {
            throw new GradleException("PMD did not produce ${report} - see the output above")
        }
        def root = new groovy.xml.XmlSlurper().parse(report)
        def violations = []
        root.file.each { f ->
            f.violation.each { v -> violations << "[ERROR] ${f.@name}:${v.@beginline}: ${v.text().trim()} [${v.@rule}]" }
        }
        def rulesetSuppressions = ['xpath', 'regex']
        root.suppressedviolation.findAll { !(it.@suppressiontype.text() in rulesetSuppressions) }.each { s ->
            violations << "[ERROR] ${s.@filename}: suppressed (${s.@suppressiontype}) - ${s.@msg} [suppression]"
        }
        root.error.each { e -> violations << "[ERROR] ${e.@filename}: PMD could not analyse the file - ${e.@msg} [error]" }
        root.configerror.each { e -> violations << "[ERROR] rule ${e.@rule}: ${e.@msg} [ruleset]" }
        violations.each { println it }
        if (violations) {
            throw new GradleException("PMD: ${violations.size()} violation(s) of gauntlet/config/pmd-ruleset.xml")
        }
        println 'PMD: OK'
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ tests

tasks.named('test') {
    mustRunAfter 'checkstyleGate', 'pmdGate'
}

tasks.register('archTest', Test) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Enforces gauntlet/config/architecture.properties with ArchUnit.'
    testClassesDirs = sourceSets.archTest.output.classesDirs
    classpath = sourceSets.archTest.runtimeClasspath
    useJUnitPlatform()
    systemProperty 'gauntlet.architecture', configFile('architecture.properties').absolutePath
    // the policy is read by the test, not handed to it: without this input a stricter policy left archTest
    // UP-TO-DATE (or FROM-CACHE after clean) on the result of the old one
    inputs.file(configFile('architecture.properties')).withPropertyName('architecturePolicy')
            .withPathSensitivity(PathSensitivity.NONE)
    testLogging { events 'failed'; exceptionFormat = 'full'; showStandardStreams = true }
    jacoco { enabled = false }
    mustRunAfter 'test'
}

// What test and archTest ran, judged by their results rather than by the build script (TestCensus.java): every test
// class compiled into a task's testClassesDirs must be in its JUnit XML results - finding T6, which only the
// integrity allowlist accepts. B2 reads the script for filters and stays the early signal; each review round found
// a form of filter it does not see (a variable, tasks['test'], matching { }, a closure parameter, a filter of the
// test platform outside the script), and the census sees the effect of all of them - and of a test framework or
// engine the task does not have (JUnit 4 tests without the vintage engine never run).
def censusTasks = ['test', 'archTest']
tasks.register('testCensus', Exec) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Fails when a test class that test or archTest compiled did not run (judged by their JUnit XML results).'
    dependsOn censusTasks
    executable javaBin
    args sourceUtf8, "${tools}/TestCensus.java", '--project-dir', projectDir.absolutePath,
            '--allowlist', configFile('integrity-allowlist.txt').absolutePath
    doFirst {
        // One results directory for both: a Test run deletes the TEST-*.xml it finds there, so archTest's run took
        // test's results away (tasks.withType(Test) { reports.junitXml.outputLocation = ... } for a CI collector).
        def xmlDirs = censusTasks.collect { tasks.getByName(it).reports.junitXml.outputLocation.get().asFile }
        if (xmlDirs.unique(false).size() < xmlDirs.size()) {
            throw new GradleException("gauntlet: test and archTest write their JUnit XML into one directory " +
                    "(${xmlDirs[0]}), and each run deletes the results already there, so the census cannot tell what " +
                    "test ran. Give each Test task a directory of its own: reports.junitXml.outputLocation = " +
                    "layout.buildDirectory.dir(\"test-results/\${name}\").")
        }
        censusTasks.each { name ->
            def task = tasks.getByName(name)
            // The results on disk are this build's only when the task is part of it: with -x test, or a build script
            // that takes the task out of the build (startParameter.excludedTaskNames), they are an earlier run's.
            if (!gradle.taskGraph.hasTask(task)) {
                throw new GradleException("gauntlet: ${task.path} is not part of this build (left out with -x, or by the " +
                        "build itself), so whether the test classes it compiled ran is unknown. Run the gauntlet with it.")
            }
            // Without the report Gradle neither writes nor deletes it: the directory keeps an earlier run's results.
            def xml = task.reports.junitXml
            if (!xml.required.get()) {
                throw new GradleException("gauntlet: testCensus judges ${task.path} by its JUnit XML results, and this build " +
                        "switches them off (reports.junitXml.required = false), so whether its test classes ran is " +
                        "unknown. Remove that setting.")
            }
            // The classes a source set compiles are what the task must run: a build that narrows testClassesDirs
            // (testClassesDirs.asFileTree.matching { exclude ... }, files()) keeps test classes out of the run, and
            // the census would judge only what is left. More directories than the source set's are judged too.
            def testSet = sourceSets.getByName(name == 'test' ? 'test' : 'archTest')
            // where the source set's compile tasks write: the build controls testClassesDirs and the source set's
            // output.classesDirs alike (output.classesDirs.setFrom(files()) emptied both), not where javac writes
            def compiled = ['java', 'kotlin', 'groovy']
                    .collect { tasks.findByName(testSet.getCompileTaskName(it))?.destinationDirectory?.getOrNull()?.asFile }
                    .findAll { it != null } as Set
            def listed = task.testClassesDirs.files
            if (!listed.containsAll(compiled)) {
                throw new GradleException("gauntlet: ${task.path} runs the test classes in ${listed ?: 'nothing'}, " +
                        "not the classes its source set compiles (${compiled.join(', ')}): a narrowed testClassesDirs " +
                        "keeps test classes out of the run. Leave testClassesDirs as the source set's output.")
            }
            // the source sets that compile into the task's classes: their roots name the source file of a class
            def dirs = listed.findAll { !it.isFile() }
            def roots = sourceSets.findAll { set -> set.output.classesDirs.files.any { it in dirs } }
                    .collectMany { it.allSource.srcDirs as List }
            args '--task', name, '--classes-file', pathList("census-${name}-classes", dirs*.absolutePath),
                    '--sources-file', pathList("census-${name}-sources", roots*.absolutePath)
            // A test source its compile task leaves out (sourceSets.test.java.exclude, compileTestJava { exclude })
            // has no class: nothing above could miss it, and nothing would ever run it. Java sources: the source
            // set's directories on disk against what the compile task compiles.
            // The conventional directory (src/test/java) counts even when the build moved the source set's
            // directories elsewhere (srcDirs = []): a test there would compile and run in a plain build.
            def compileInputs = tasks.getByName(testSet.compileJavaTaskName).source.files
            def notCompiled = ((testSet.java.srcDirs as List) + [file("src/${testSet.name}/java")]).unique()
                    .findAll { it.isDirectory() }
                    .collectMany { dir -> fileTree(dir) { include '**/*.java' }.files as List }.unique()
                    .findAll { !(it.name in ['package-info.java', 'module-info.java']) && !(it in compileInputs) }
            args '--not-compiled-file', pathList("census-${name}-not-compiled", notCompiled*.absolutePath)
            // Executed, UP-TO-DATE or FROM-CACHE: the directory holds the results of these very inputs (a run deletes
            // the TEST-*.xml an earlier one wrote; the filters are inputs). SKIPPED (onlyIf, enabled = false): the
            // task ran nothing in this build, whatever an earlier run left there.
            def outcome = task.state.skipped ? task.state.skipMessage : null
            if (outcome in [null, 'UP-TO-DATE', 'FROM-CACHE']) {
                args '--results', xml.outputLocation.get().asFile.absolutePath
            } else {
                args '--not-run', outcome
            }
        }
    }
}

def configureCucumber = { Test task, File features ->
    task.testClassesDirs = sourceSets.acceptanceTest.output.classesDirs
    task.classpath = sourceSets.acceptanceTest.runtimeClasspath
    task.useJUnitPlatform { includeEngines 'cucumber' }
    // cucumber.features is a comma-separated list: a directory under "/home/me/Acme, Inc" goes relative to the
    // project directory, where its test JVM then starts
    if (features.absolutePath.contains(',')) {
        task.workingDir = projectDir
        task.systemProperty 'cucumber.features', relativeTo(projectDir, features)
    } else {
        task.systemProperty 'cucumber.features', features.absolutePath
    }
    task.systemProperty 'cucumber.publish.quiet', 'true'
    if (glue) {
        task.systemProperty 'cucumber.glue', glue
    }
}
def hasFeatures = { File dir -> dir.exists() && Files.walk(dir.toPath()).withCloseable { s -> s.anyMatch { it.toString().endsWith('.feature') } } }

// Cucumber's message stream (cucumber.plugin message:FILE) is the record of what a run did: every scenario it ran, the
// feature file and line it came from, when it started and when it finished. acceptanceCheck counts it against the
// scenarios the feature files define, gherkinMutation judges by it the order the mutants ran in - what the run did,
// whatever its settings said. One stream per test JVM: a retry (the test-retry plugin) runs each round in a JVM of its
// own, which would write the file anew. So a JVM's stream moves aside once Gradle reports the JVM done - its suite
// right below the root of the run ("Gradle Test Executor 2"), which Gradle reports before it starts the next round.
def cucumberMessages = { Test task, File dir ->
    def current = new File(dir, 'current.ndjson')
    def jvms = 0
    task.outputs.dir(dir).withPropertyName('cucumberMessages')
    task.doFirst {
        dir.deleteDir()
        dir.mkdirs()
    }
    task.afterSuite { TestDescriptor suite, TestResult result ->
        if (suite.parent != null && suite.parent.parent == null && current.isFile()) {
            Files.move(current.toPath(), new File(dir, "jvm-${++jvms}.ndjson").toPath())
        }
    }
    return current
}
// junit-platform.properties of one classpath entry (a directory or a jar), or null
def platformProperties = { File entry ->
    def properties = null
    if (entry.isDirectory() && new File(entry, 'junit-platform.properties').isFile()) {
        properties = new Properties()
        new File(entry, 'junit-platform.properties').withInputStream { properties.load(it) }
    } else if (entry.isFile() && entry.name.endsWith('.jar')) {
        try {
            new java.util.zip.ZipFile(entry).withCloseable { jar ->
                def found = jar.getEntry('junit-platform.properties')
                if (found != null) {
                    properties = new Properties()
                    jar.getInputStream(found).withCloseable { properties.load(it) }
                }
            }
        } catch (java.util.zip.ZipException notAJar) {     // the class loader skips it as well
        }
    }
    return properties
}
// The cucumber.plugin of the task's test JVMs: the project's own plugins stay - of a system property of the task, else
// of the first junit-platform.properties on its classpath, where JUnit Platform reads them - and the stream joins them.
// Gradle keeps a -D of jvmArgs as a system property, so it stays; a project's argument provider is overridden.
// Cucumber splits the list at commas: a stream under a directory named with one goes relative to the working
// directory of the JVM.
def cucumberPlugins = { Test task, File stream ->
    def own = task.systemProperties['cucumber.plugin']?.toString()
    if (own == null) {
        own = task.classpath.files.findResult { platformProperties(it) }?.getProperty('cucumber.plugin')
    }
    def path = stream.absolutePath.contains(',') ? relativeTo(task.workingDir, stream) : stream.absolutePath
    // entry by entry: Cucumber alone drops an empty last entry (`pretty,`), but not one in the middle of a list
    def plugins = (own ?: '').split(',').collect { it.trim() }.findAll { it }
    return '-Dcucumber.plugin=' + (plugins + ['message:' + path]).join(', ')
}
// What the gates need of every Cucumber run they judge, whatever the project's settings say. The steps execute: a dry
// run (cucumber.execution.dry-run) reports every step passed without running the glue, and the stream cannot tell.
// Cucumber discovers the features as the root engine: a @Suite setup turns that off, and then no scenario runs.
def cucumberRun = ['cucumber.execution.dry-run': 'false', 'cucumber.junit-platform.discovery.as-root-engine': 'true']
// the last -D the test JVM of a finished Test task got for a key, as Gradle lists the arguments
def lastSystemProperty = { Test task, String key ->
    def values = task.allJvmArgs.findAll { it.startsWith("-D${key}=") }
    values ? values[-1].substring(key.length() + 3) : 'unset'
}
// _JAVA_OPTIONS of the test JVM's environment: the JVM reads it after the command line, so a -Dcucumber.* there beats
// every -D the kit passes (dry-run, the plugin, the order), and Gradle's argument list does not show it
def cucumberInJavaOptions = { Test task ->
    def options = task.environment['_JAVA_OPTIONS']?.toString() ?: ''
    (options =~ /-Dcucumber\.[^\s=]+=?\S*/).collect { "_JAVA_OPTIONS ${it}".toString() }
}
def acceptanceMessages = buildDirFile('cucumber-messages/acceptanceTest')

tasks.register('acceptanceTest', Test) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Runs the Gherkin acceptance tests (Cucumber) from ' + featuresPath
    configureCucumber(it, featuresDir)
    // the features are passed as a system property, which Gradle does not track by content: without this
    // input a change to only the feature files leaves acceptanceTest UP-TO-DATE and the new spec never runs.
    inputs.dir(featuresDir).optional().withPathSensitivity(PathSensitivity.RELATIVE)
    testLogging { events 'failed'; exceptionFormat = 'full' }
    onlyIf { task -> hasFeatures(featuresDir) || skippedByTheKit(task, 'no feature file') }
    mustRunAfter 'archTest'
    finalizedBy 'acceptanceCheck'
    // acceptanceCheck must judge this run only, never results a previous run left behind
    def results = reports.junitXml.outputLocation.get().asFile
    doFirst { results.deleteDir(); results.mkdirs() }
    def stream = cucumberMessages(it, acceptanceMessages)
    doFirst { Test task ->
        // Cucumber finds the scenarios by cucumber.features, not by the test classes Gradle hands each fork: forks in
        // parallel (a maxParallelForks for every Test task) each ran every scenario, at the same time, and wrote one
        // message stream at once. One at a time, every fork still runs them all.
        task.maxParallelForks = 1
        // at execution, as for gherkinMutantsRun: the provider reads the project's plugins as the JVM will get them
        task.jvmArgumentProviders.add({ cucumberRun.collect { key, value -> "-D${key}=${value}".toString() } +
                [cucumberPlugins(task, stream)] } as CommandLineArgumentProvider)
    }
    // After the run, where no doFirst can change them any more: a doFirst of the project's own that drops the kit's
    // provider (one registered before apply from) would let a dry run pass every scenario.
    doLast { Test task ->
        def wrong = cucumberRun.findAll { key, value -> lastSystemProperty(task, key) != value }
                .collect { key, value -> "${key}=${lastSystemProperty(task, key)}" } + cucumberInJavaOptions(task)
        if (wrong) {
            throw new GradleException("gauntlet: acceptanceTest ran with ${wrong.join(', ')}: the gates judge scenarios " +
                    "whose steps executed. A doFirst of the project's own changed what the kit set (one registered " +
                    "before apply from: tasks.withType(Test), a convention plugin, allprojects, an init script), or " +
                    "_JAVA_OPTIONS of the task's environment overrides it - keep both off acceptanceTest.")
        }
    }
}

tasks.register('acceptanceCheck', Exec) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Fails when scenarios were skipped (aborted by an assumption or a skipped step) - Gradle would pass them - ' +
            'when feature files exist but no scenario ran, or when a scenario they define did not run.'
    def results = buildDirFile('test-results/acceptanceTest')
    executable javaBin
    args sourceUtf8, "${tools}/GherkinMutator.java", 'no-skipped', '--results', results.absolutePath,
            '--features', featuresDir.absolutePath, '--messages', acceptanceMessages.absolutePath,
            '--root', projectDir.absolutePath, '--allowlist', configFile('integrity-allowlist.txt').absolutePath
    doFirst {
        // The results and the stream on disk are this build's only when acceptanceTest is part of it and ran (or is
        // UP-TO-DATE on these very inputs): left out with -x, they are an earlier run's; skipped (a project's onlyIf,
        // enabled = false), they are gone - then no scenario ran.
        def acceptance = tasks.getByName('acceptanceTest')
        if (!gradle.taskGraph.hasTask(acceptance)) {
            throw new GradleException("gauntlet: acceptanceCheck judges the acceptance run of this build, and " +
                    "${acceptance.path} is not part of it (left out with -x, or not asked for): run them together.")
        }
        if (acceptance.state.skipped && !(acceptance.state.skipMessage in ['UP-TO-DATE', 'FROM-CACHE'])) {
            results.deleteDir()
            acceptanceMessages.deleteDir()
        }
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ CRAP and DRY

jacoco {
    toolVersion = setting('jacoco.version', '0.8.15')
}
def jacocoExcludes = excludedClassGlobs.collectMany { ["**/${it}.class", "**/${it}\$*.class"] }
tasks.named('jacocoTestReport', JacocoReport) {
    dependsOn 'test'
    reports {
        xml.required = true
        html.required = true
    }
    classDirectories.setFrom(files(sourceSets.main.output.classesDirs.files.collect { dir ->
        fileTree(dir) { exclude jacocoExcludes }
    }))
}

tasks.register('crapGate', Exec) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'CRAP = CC^2 * (1 - coverage)^3 + CC per method; fails above crap.threshold.'
    dependsOn 'jacocoTestReport', 'gauntletScope'
    mustRunAfter 'acceptanceTest'
    executable javaBin
    args sourceUtf8, "${tools}/CrapGate.java", '--report', buildDirFile('reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml').absolutePath,
            '--threshold', setting('crap.threshold', '8'), '--allowlist', configFile('crap-allowlist.txt').absolutePath,
            '--exclude', excludedClassGlobs.join(',')
    doFirst {
        args '--encoding', sourceEncoding()
        def only = changedSources()
        if (only != null) {
            requireChangedClasses()             // CrapGate derives the changed types the same way
            args '--only-file', pathList('crap-changed-sources', only*.path)
            sourceSets.main.java.srcDirs.each { args '--sources', it.absolutePath }                  // one root each
        }
    }
}

tasks.register('cpdReport', JavaExec) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Runs PMD CPD (copy/paste detector) over the main sources.'
    def report = buildDirFile('reports/cpd/cpd.xml')
    classpath = configurations.gauntletCpd
    mainClass = 'net.sourceforge.pmd.cli.PmdCli'
    args 'cpd', '--language', 'java', '--minimum-tokens', setting('dry.minimumTokens', '60'), '--format', 'xml',
            '--report-file', report.absolutePath, '--no-fail-on-violation', '--ignore-annotations'
    if (setting('dry.ignoreIdentifiers', 'true').toBoolean()) {
        args '--ignore-identifiers'
    }
    if (setting('dry.ignoreLiterals', 'true').toBoolean()) {
        args '--ignore-literals'
    }
    // paths (files or directories) relative to the module, left out of the duplicate search (CLI --exclude, CPD 7.0+)
    listSetting('dry.exclude', '').each { args '--exclude', file(it).absolutePath }
    // every root of the main source set; the roots and the charset are inputs, known when the task is about to run
    def roots = providers.provider { mainSourceRoots().findAll { it.exists() } }
    inputs.files(roots).withPropertyName('mainSourceRoots')
    inputs.property('sourceEncoding', providers.provider { sourceEncoding() })
    outputs.file(report)
    onlyIf { task -> !roots.get().isEmpty() || skippedByTheKit(task, 'no main source root') }
    doFirst {
        // positional after "--": CPD splits a --dir value at commas, not a positional one (see pmdGate)
        args(['--encoding', sourceEncoding(), '--'] + roots.get()*.absolutePath)
        report.parentFile.mkdirs()
    }
}

tasks.register('dryGate', Exec) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Fails on duplicated code (in scope: duplications touching a changed file).'
    dependsOn 'cpdReport', 'gauntletScope'
    mustRunAfter 'crapGate'
    executable javaBin
    args sourceUtf8, "${tools}/DryGate.java", '--report', buildDirFile('reports/cpd/cpd.xml').absolutePath,
            '--project-dir', projectDir.absolutePath, '--max', setting('dry.maxDuplications', '0')
    doFirst {
        def only = changedMainJava()
        if (only != null) {
            args '--only-file', pathList('dry-changed-sources', only)
        }
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ mutation testing

def pit = [applied: false]
plugins.withId('info.solidsoft.pitest') {
    pit.applied = true
    pitest {
        pitestVersion = setting('pit.version', '1.22.1')
        junit5PluginVersion = setting('pit.junit5PluginVersion', '1.2.3')
        // The plugin would add its own org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher to the test runtime classpath; when
        // the JUnit version is managed by a BOM (Spring Boot) rather than declared literally it falls back to a
        // hard-coded 1.x launcher, which cannot drive a JUnit 6 engine ("OutputDirectoryCreator not available") and
        // breaks ./gradlew test. The project declares the launcher itself (testRuntimeOnly), BOM-aligned.
        addJUnitPlatformLauncher = false
        threads = setting('pit.threads', '4').toInteger()
        mutators = listSetting('pit.mutators', 'DEFAULTS') as Set
        outputFormats = ['XML', 'HTML'] as Set
        timestampedReports = false
        // No history (build/pitHistory.txt): PIT's incremental analysis keeps a KILLED verdict while the mutated class
        // and the killing test's class are unchanged, and a SURVIVED one while the covering test classes are. A test
        // weakened through a helper class or a test resource kept its kills, and the hardener's SubagentStop hook let
        // the survivor through; a test sharpened that way kept its survivor. A history the project sets through the
        // plugin is refused when pitest runs (its doFirst below).
        enableDefaultIncrementalAnalysis = false
        excludedGroups = listSetting('pit.excludedGroups', 'no-mutate') as Set
        // nested classes too, as JaCoCo (jacocoExcludes) and CrapGate (outer class name) already do
        excludedClasses = excludedClassGlobs.collectMany { [it, it + '$*'] } as Set
        // Uncle Bob's rule: every COVERED mutant is killed (PIT test strength). maxSurviving would also count
        // uncovered mutants; uncovered code is policed by coverageThreshold (line coverage of mutated classes).
        testStrengthThreshold = setting('pit.testStrengthThreshold', '100').toInteger()
        coverageThreshold = setting('pit.coverageThreshold', '0').toInteger()
        failWhenNoMutations = false
        if (basePackage) {
            targetClasses = ["${basePackage}.*".toString()] as Set
            // must be explicit: by default the plugin uses targetClasses as targetTests, and with a changed-class
            // scope that would exclude FooTest when mutating Foo - every mutant would look uncovered
            targetTests = ["${basePackage}.*".toString()] as Set
        }
    }
    tasks.named('pitest') {
        group = 'gauntlet'
        dependsOn 'gauntletScope'
        mustRunAfter 'crapGate', 'dryGate', 'acceptanceTest'
        finalizedBy 'pitSummary'
        def staleReport = buildDirFile('reports/pitest/mutations.xml')
        def pkg = basePackage
        doFirst {
            staleReport.delete()
            if (!pkg) {
                throw new GradleException('gauntlet: set basePackage in gauntlet/config/gauntlet.properties')
            }
            // The plugin hands PIT the class directories to mutate as one comma-separated list (--mutableCodePaths),
            // and PIT splits it: under "/home/me/Acme, Inc" it found "No mutations" and the gate passed on nothing.
            def split = mutableCodePaths.files.find { it.absolutePath.contains(',') }
            if (split) {
                throw new GradleException("gauntlet: PIT would read ${split} as two paths at its comma and find nothing " +
                        "to mutate. Build from a directory without a comma in its path.")
            }
            // The plugin hands PIT the project's own history files with the flag above off as well, and the project can
            // turn the flag on again: a weakened test kept its kills and mutationGate passed. Judged as the task has
            // them now (pitest {} or the task, before this script, after it, in afterEvaluate) and fixed: a doFirst of
            // the project's that runs after this one can no longer set them.
            [historyInputLocation, historyOutputLocation, enableDefaultIncrementalAnalysis]*.finalizeValue()
            def flag = enableDefaultIncrementalAnalysis.getOrElse(false)
            def history = [historyInputLocation: historyInputLocation.present,
                           historyOutputLocation: historyOutputLocation.present,
                           'enableDefaultIncrementalAnalysis (withHistory)': flag].findAll { it.value }.keySet()
            if (history) {
                throw new GradleException("gauntlet: PIT incremental analysis is configured for this build (" +
                        "${history.join(', ')}): PIT would keep the verdicts of an earlier run, and a test weakened " +
                        "since would keep its kills. Remove it from pitest { } and the pitest task - in the build script, a convention " +
                        "plugin or an init script.")
            }
        }
        if (scope != 'all') {
            // the changed types are known when the task is about to run (gauntletScope and the compiler ran)
            targetClasses.set(providers.provider { changedClassGlobs() as Set })
            onlyIf { task ->
                changedClassGlobs() || changedClassProblems() || skippedByTheKit(task, 'no changed main class')
            }
            doFirst { requireChangedClasses() }   // a wrongly derived target would make PIT find "no mutations" and pass
        }
    }
}

tasks.register('pitSummary', Exec) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Lists surviving, uncovered and unverified (RUN_ERROR) mutants and oversized files from the PIT ' +
            'report; fails on a RUN_ERROR mutant outside config/pit-runerror-allowlist.txt.'
    onlyIf { task -> scope == 'all' || changedClassGlobs() || skippedByTheKit(task, 'no changed main class') }
    executable javaBin
    args sourceUtf8, "${tools}/PitSummary.java", '--report', buildDirFile('reports/pitest/mutations.xml').absolutePath,
            '--max-per-file', setting('pit.maxMutationsPerFile', '100'),
            '--allowlist', configFile('pit-runerror-allowlist.txt').absolutePath
}

tasks.register('mutationGate') {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Mutation testing with PIT: every covered mutant in scope must be killed, and a RUN_ERROR mutant ' +
            '(PIT counts it as detected, the tests never ran) only passes through config/pit-runerror-allowlist.txt.'
    if (pit.applied) {
        dependsOn 'pitest', 'pitSummary'
    }
    def applied = pit.applied
    doLast {
        if (!applied) {
            throw new GradleException("mutationGate needs the PIT plugin: add id(\"info.solidsoft.pitest\") version \"1.19.0\" to plugins {}")
        }
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Gherkin mutation

def mutantsDir = buildDirFile('gherkin-mutation/mutants')
def mutantResults = buildDirFile('gherkin-mutation/results')
def mutantMessages = buildDirFile('gherkin-mutation/messages')

tasks.register('gherkinMutants', Exec) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Generates one feature file per mutated Examples value.'
    dependsOn 'acceptanceTest', 'gauntletScope'
    if (pit.applied) {
        mustRunAfter 'pitest'
    }
    executable javaBin
    args sourceUtf8, "${tools}/GherkinMutator.java", 'generate', '--features', featuresPath, '--out', mutantsDir.absolutePath
    doFirst {
        def changed = changedFiles()
        if (changed != null) {
            // The step definitions are what this gate checks: a changed glue file or acceptance resource can hollow
            // a step of a feature that did not change, so then every feature is mutated. Deleting a glue file (a
            // hook, a step class) or moving it away changes the glue as well: both ends of a rename count.
            def touched = (gitPaths(['diff', '-z', '--relative', '--name-only', '--no-renames', mergeBase()]) ?: []) + changed
            def roots = sourceSets.acceptanceTest.allSource.srcDirs.collect { it.toPath().toAbsolutePath().normalize() }
            def changedGlue = touched.unique().findAll { path ->
                !path.endsWith('.feature') && roots.any { file(path).toPath().toAbsolutePath().normalize().startsWith(it) }
            }
            if (changedGlue) {
                logger.lifecycle("gauntlet: ${changedGlue.size()} acceptance glue file(s) changed (" +
                        "${changedGlue.take(3).join(', ')}${changedGlue.size() > 3 ? ', ...' : ''}) - every feature is mutated")
            } else {
                args '--only-file', pathList('changed-features', changedFeatures())
            }
        }
    }
}

tasks.register('gherkinMutantsRun', Test) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Runs the generated mutant scenarios; failures are the expected outcome.'
    dependsOn 'gherkinMutants'
    configureCucumber(it, mutantsDir)
    systemProperty 'cucumber.junit-platform.naming-strategy', 'long'
    ignoreFailures = true
    reports.junitXml.outputLocation.set(mutantResults)
    reports.html.required = false
    outputs.upToDateWhen { false }
    jacoco { enabled = false }
    onlyIf { task -> hasFeatures(mutantsDir) || skippedByTheKit(task, 'no Examples value in scope') }
    def stream = cucumberMessages(it, mutantMessages)
    doFirst { Test task ->
        // failing scenarios are what this run is for: a project-wide failFast would stop it after the first kill
        failFast = false
        // The controls of a row run before its mutants and after them (GherkinMutator generate): one JVM, one scenario
        // at a time, the files in the order of their names - not as the project runs its own acceptance tests (in
        // junit-platform.properties, where a system property wins, or in tasks.withType(Test)). In parallel both
        // controls ran first, and a stand that wears out (a quota) failed the mutant instead: a kill.
        maxParallelForks = 1
        forkEvery = 0
        // an argument provider added at execution: the test JVM gets one -D per key, and a provider's beats the
        // project's jvmArgs and systemProperty, even ones its own doFirst sets after this one. The message stream
        // records what the run did with them (gherkinMutation judges the order by it).
        jvmArgumentProviders.add({ ['-Dcucumber.execution.parallel.enabled=false', '-Dcucumber.execution.order=lexical'] +
                cucumberRun.collect { key, value -> "-D${key}=${value}".toString() } +
                [cucumberPlugins(task, stream)] } as CommandLineArgumentProvider)
        // Gradle 8.14 lists the report directory without creating it: recreate it after the wipe
        mutantResults.deleteDir()
        mutantResults.mkdirs()
    }
    // A doFirst registered before this script (tasks.withType(Test) above the apply line, a convention plugin,
    // allprojects, an init script) runs after the one above: its forks went through, and its own provider won - the
    // mutants ran in parallel or in a random order, and the gate passed. So the settings are judged here, after the
    // test action (it returns when mutants fail: ignoreFailures), where no doFirst can change them any more. Unset
    // counts as wrong: the kit's provider was removed. The arguments are the ones Gradle lists: _JAVA_OPTIONS in the
    // task's environment, an argument file, a provider that answers differently after the run or a doLast of the
    // project that restores the settings are not seen here - gherkinMutation judges the order the scenarios really
    // ran in, from Cucumber's message stream. This check stays the early message that names the setting.
    doLast {
        def last = { String key ->
            def values = allJvmArgs.findAll { it.startsWith("-D${key}=") }
            values ? values[-1].substring(key.length() + 3) : 'unset'
        }
        def used = [maxParallelForks: maxParallelForks, forkEvery: forkEvery,
                    'cucumber.execution.parallel.enabled': last('cucumber.execution.parallel.enabled'),
                    'cucumber.execution.order': last('cucumber.execution.order')] +
                cucumberRun.collectEntries { key, value -> [(key): last(key)] }
        def wrong = ([maxParallelForks: 1, forkEvery: 0, 'cucumber.execution.parallel.enabled': 'false',
                      'cucumber.execution.order': 'lexical'] + cucumberRun).findAll { key, value -> used[key] != value }
                .collect { key, value -> "${key}=${used[key]}" } + cucumberInJavaOptions(it)
        if (wrong) {
            throw new GradleException("gauntlet: gherkinMutantsRun ran with ${wrong.join(', ')}: its controls prove " +
                    "nothing unless one JVM runs one scenario at a time, in the order of the file names. A doFirst " +
                    "of the project's own changed what the kit set (one registered before apply from: " +
                    "tasks.withType(Test), a convention plugin, allprojects, an init script), or _JAVA_OPTIONS of " +
                    "the task's environment overrides it - keep both off gherkinMutantsRun.")
        }
    }
}

tasks.register('gherkinMutation', Exec) {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Gherkin acceptance mutation: every mutated Examples value must make a scenario fail.'
    dependsOn 'gherkinMutantsRun'
    executable javaBin
    args sourceUtf8, "${tools}/GherkinMutator.java", 'verdict', '--mutants', mutantsDir.absolutePath, '--results', mutantResults.absolutePath,
            '--messages', mutantMessages.absolutePath
    // The glue the mutant run loaded, as compiled - its classpath (configureCucumber): a failure thrown by a transformer
    // (@ParameterType, ...) is a rejected value, not a kill. Cucumber names a glue method by its class and method, and
    // so does the verdict: the language of the glue and the encoding of its sources do not matter. The entries go as
    // a list file (see pathList): a classpath can be long, and a path can hold any separator.
    def glueClasspath = sourceSets.acceptanceTest.runtimeClasspath
    doFirst { args '--glue-file', pathList('glue-classpath', glueClasspath.files*.absolutePath) }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ aggregates

// A gate's verdict is its tool's exit code. A build that sets ignoreExitValue on them (tasks.withType(Exec) { ... }
// before the kit) let every finding pass; judged after the run, where no doFirst can change the setting any more.
// checkstyleGate and pmdGate ignore the exit value themselves and judge their XML reports.
['integrityCheck', 'testCensus', 'acceptanceCheck', 'crapGate', 'cpdReport', 'dryGate', 'pitSummary', 'gherkinMutants',
 'gherkinMutation'].each { name ->
    tasks.named(name) { task ->
        task.doLast {
            def exit = task.executionResult.getOrNull()?.exitValue
            if (exit != null && exit != 0) {
                throw new GradleException("gauntlet: ${task.path} ended with exit value ${exit}, and the build ignores " +
                        "exit values (ignoreExitValue = true): a gate's verdict is its tool's exit code. Remove that " +
                        "setting.")
            }
        }
    }
}

tasks.register('gauntletFast') {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'Integrity, checkstyle, PMD, unit, architecture and acceptance tests, the test census, CRAP, DRY.'
    dependsOn 'gauntletScope', 'integrityCheck', 'checkstyleGate', 'pmdGate', 'test', 'archTest', 'testCensus',
            'acceptanceTest', 'acceptanceCheck', 'crapGate', 'dryGate'
}

tasks.register('gauntlet') {
    group = 'gauntlet'
    description = 'The whole gauntlet: gauntletFast + mutationGate + gherkinMutation.'
    dependsOn 'gauntletFast', 'mutationGate', 'gherkinMutation'
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ one run per build directory

// Two Gradle runs in the same build/ (the agent's own run in the background, a Stop hook, a subagent's run)
// overwrite each other's classes, test results and reports: a gate can then judge a half-written or foreign
// result. Every task of this build therefore holds an exclusive OS file lock on .gradle/gauntlet-build.lock
// (outside build/, so clean cannot delete it from under a holder) from its first action until the build ends;
// a second run waits for it. Gradle closes the service after the last task that uses it (Gradle 8.14 user guide,
// "Using Shared Build Services"), which releases the lock.
abstract class GauntletBuildLock implements BuildService<GauntletBuildLock.Params>, AutoCloseable {
    interface Params extends BuildServiceParameters {
        Property<String> getLockPath()
        Property<Integer> getWaitSeconds()
    }

    private java.nio.channels.FileChannel channel
    private java.nio.channels.FileLock lock

    synchronized void hold(String taskPath) {
        if (lock != null) {
            return
        }
        def file = new File(parameters.lockPath.get())
        file.parentFile.mkdirs()
        channel = java.nio.channels.FileChannel.open(file.toPath(), java.nio.file.StandardOpenOption.CREATE,
                java.nio.file.StandardOpenOption.READ, java.nio.file.StandardOpenOption.WRITE)
        long deadline = System.currentTimeMillis() + parameters.waitSeconds.get() * 1000L
        boolean told = false
        while ((lock = tryLock()) == null) {
            if (System.currentTimeMillis() > deadline) {
                channel.close()
                channel = null
                throw new GradleException("[gauntlet] another Gradle run (${holder(file)}) has been using this build " +
                        "directory for over ${parameters.waitSeconds.get()} s - wait for it to finish, then run again.")
            }
            if (!told) {
                println "[gauntlet] ${taskPath}: another Gradle run (${holder(file)}) is using this build directory - waiting for it"
                told = true
            }
            Thread.sleep(2000)
        }
        channel.truncate(0)
        // the daemon runs on the project's JDK, which may be Java 8: no ProcessHandle (Java 9+) in this script
        def pid = java.lang.management.ManagementFactory.runtimeMXBean.name.split('@')[0]
        channel.write(java.nio.ByteBuffer.wrap("pid ${pid}".getBytes('UTF-8')), 0)
        channel.force(false)
    }

    // a lock another build of the same JVM (daemon) still holds shows up as an exception, not as null
    private java.nio.channels.FileLock tryLock() {
        try {
            return channel.tryLock()
        } catch (java.nio.channels.OverlappingFileLockException ignored) {
            return null
        }
    }

    private static String holder(File file) {
        try {
            return file.getText('UTF-8').trim() ?: 'pid unknown'
        } catch (IOException ignored) {
            return 'pid unknown'
        }
    }

    @Override
    void close() {
        lock?.release()
        channel?.close()
    }
}

def buildLock = gradle.sharedServices.registerIfAbsent('gauntletBuildLock-' + projectDir.absolutePath.md5(), GauntletBuildLock) {
    parameters.lockPath = new File(projectDir, '.gradle/gauntlet-build.lock').absolutePath
    parameters.waitSeconds = (findProperty('gauntlet.lockWaitSeconds') ?: '1500').toString().toInteger()
}
tasks.configureEach { Task task ->
    task.usesService(buildLock)
    def path = task.path
    task.doFirst { buildLock.get().hold(path) }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ gate JVM

// The gate JVM is the last word on these tasks, whatever the project says about its Test/JavaExec tasks before
// this script, after it or in afterEvaluate: the configuration is added once every project is evaluated. (Later
// is too late - Gradle fixes the launcher of a task when it puts the task into the task graph.) Gradle also keeps
// a launcher that was read once the project is evaluated, and an init script's projectsEvaluated runs before this
// one: so the gate JVM is set as well when a task is created (for what reads launchers in afterEvaluate - an IDE's
// model builder, an init script) and after the project's own afterEvaluate actions (an action added from inside
// afterEvaluate runs after all of them), over a launcher the project pinned there.
def gateTasks = ['checkstyleGate', 'pmdGate', 'cpdReport', 'acceptanceTest', 'archTest', 'gherkinMutantsRun',
                 'integrityCheck', 'testCensus', 'acceptanceCheck', 'crapGate', 'dryGate', 'pitSummary', 'gherkinMutants',
                 'gherkinMutation']
def gateJvmOfTasks = { ->
    gateTasks.each { tasks.named(it) { gateJvmOf(it) } }
    plugins.withId('info.solidsoft.pitest') {
        tasks.named('pitest') { gateJvmOf(it) }
    }
}
gateJvmOfTasks()
afterEvaluate { afterEvaluate { gateJvmOfTasks() } }
gradle.projectsEvaluated {
    gateTasks.each { tasks.named(it) { gateJava(it) } }
    plugins.withId('info.solidsoft.pitest') {
        tasks.named('pitest') { gateJava(it) }
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ configuration cache

// A project may enable the configuration cache (org.gradle.configuration-cache=true in gradle.properties).
// Several gauntlet tasks read the project while they run (file() in onlyIf, sourceSets and javaLauncher in
// doFirst), which the cache forbids. They opt out explicitly (Task.notCompatibleWithConfigurationCache): a build
// that runs any of them discards its cache entry instead of failing; the project's own builds keep the cache.
def notCacheable = { Task task -> task.notCompatibleWithConfigurationCache('gauntlet tasks read the project at execution time') }
['gauntletInfo', 'gauntletScope', 'integrityCheck', 'checkstyleGate', 'pmdGate', 'archTest', 'testCensus', 'acceptanceTest',
 'acceptanceCheck', 'crapGate', 'cpdReport', 'dryGate', 'pitSummary', 'mutationGate', 'gherkinMutants',
 'gherkinMutantsRun', 'gherkinMutation', 'gauntletFast', 'gauntlet'].each { tasks.named(it, notCacheable) }
plugins.withId('info.solidsoft.pitest') { tasks.named('pitest', notCacheable) }

===== END FILE gauntlet/gauntlet.gradle =====

===== BEGIN FILE gauntlet/hooks/guard.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PreToolUse guard for the gauntlet (Claude Code hook).

Keeps agents from changing their own constraints:
  1. nobody edits the gauntlet itself (gauntlet/, .claude/, CLAUDE.md, the CI workflows), what the other agent tools
     read as their instructions, roles, settings and hooks (AGENTS.md, .codex/, .gemini/, .agents/, .grok/,
     .kimi-code/, .qwen/, .mcp.json, ...) or the user-level configuration of the agent tools (~/.claude/, ~/.codex/,
     ~/.gemini/, ~/.agents/, ~/.grok/, ~/.kimi-code/, ~/.qwen/, ~/.env, ...), which could switch the hooks off;
  2. only the `specifier` subagent writes the Gherkin specification, and once the specification is
     committed on the branch (= approved by the human in the chat) it is frozen for every agent;
  3. role scopes: specifier -> specs only, hardener -> test code only, reviewer and checker -> read-only;
  4. human-only actions are refused: merging the PR, rewriting or re-pointing the branch (--amend,
     rebase, force push, reset/checkout -B/branch -f to another revision), pushing to the base branch,
     --no-verify, core.hooksPath, git aliases and config includes (they hide any of the above), switching
     the hooks, the CI gate or the branch protection off.

Shell commands are checked heuristically: every path-like token of a command that writes to the working
tree is resolved (following `cd` and `git -C`, expanding globs) and compared with the protected paths.
A determined agent could still find a way; the integrity check, CI and the human's PR review are the
backstop. The hook fails open on malformed input so a broken hook never bricks a session.

Maintenance without the guard (humans only): set GAUNTLET_GUARD=off in the environment the session
starts with - locally `GAUNTLET_GUARD=off claude`, in the cloud an environment variable of a
separate "admin" cloud environment (see gauntlet/README.md).
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import shlex
import signal
import subprocess
import sys

HUMAN_OWNED = ("gauntlet/", ".claude/", "CLAUDE.md", ".github/workflows/gauntlet.yml",
               ".github/workflows/gauntlet-kit.yml", ".github/CODEOWNERS", ".gitlab/CODEOWNERS", "CODEOWNERS", ".git/",
               # what the other agent tools read as their instructions, roles, settings, hooks, rules and skills
               # (gauntlet/adapters/<vendor>.md): Codex, Antigravity, Grok Build, Kimi Code (agents.md is AGENTS.md in
               # another letter case), Qwen Code with the ignore files that decide what its tools see, and the
               # project's MCP servers, whose commands Kimi Code (in a trusted folder) and Claude Code (once approved)
               # start with a session, outside any tool hook
               "AGENTS.md", "AGENTS.override.md", ".codex/", "GEMINI.md", ".gemini/", ".agents/", ".grok/",
               ".kimi-code/", "QWEN.md", ".qwen/", ".qwenignore", ".agentignore", ".aiignore", ".mcp.json")
PROPERTIES = "gauntlet/config/gauntlet.properties"
DEFAULT_FEATURES = "src/acceptanceTest/resources/features"
DEFAULT_BASE = "origin/main"
TEST_CODE = ("src/test/", "src/acceptanceTest/java/")
GIT_VALUE_OPTIONS = {"-m", "-F", "-C", "-c", "-t", "--message", "--file", "--author", "--date", "--template",
                     "--reuse-message", "--reedit-message", "--fixup", "--squash", "--trailer"}
HOOK_SWITCH = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s;&|(])(?:(?:export|unset)\s+GAUNTLET_(?:GUARD|STOP_HOOK)\b|GAUNTLET_(?:GUARD|STOP_HOOK)=)")
QUOTED = re.compile(r"'[^']*'|\"(?:\\.|[^\"\\])*\"")
MUTATING_COMMANDS = {"mv", "cp", "rm", "rmdir", "truncate", "tee", "ln", "chmod", "chown", "touch", "dd",
                     "install", "patch", "unzip", "tar", "rsync", "vi", "vim", "nvim", "nano", "emacs", "ed", "ex",
                     "mkdir", "shred"}
# git subcommands that rewrite files in the working tree (checked against protected paths) ...
GIT_WORKTREE_WRITING = {"checkout", "switch", "restore", "rm", "mv", "apply", "stash", "reset", "clean", "am",
                        "cherry-pick", "revert", "merge", "rebase", "pull"}
# ... and the ones that only change git state (forbidden to the read-only reviewer and checker, fine for others)
GIT_STATE_CHANGING = GIT_WORKTREE_WRITING | {"commit", "add", "push", "tag", "branch", "update-ref", "replace",
                                             "filter-branch", "filter-repo", "notes", "worktree", "submodule"}
GIT_READ_ONLY_FORMS = {"branch": ("--show-current", "--list", "--all", "--remotes", "--verbose", "--contains",
                                  "--no-contains", "--merged", "--no-merged", "--points-at", "--format", "--sort",
                                  "--color", "--no-color", "--column", "--no-column", "--ignore-case", "--abbrev",
                                  "--no-abbrev", "--omit-empty"),
                       "stash": ("list", "show"),
                       "tag": ("--list", "--contains", "--no-contains", "--merged", "--no-merged", "--points-at",
                               "--format", "--sort", "--color", "--no-color", "--column", "--no-column", "--ignore-case"),
                       "worktree": ("list",), "notes": ("list", "show"), "submodule": ("status",)}
HISTORY_REWRITING = {"rebase", "filter-branch", "filter-repo", "update-ref", "replace", "revert"}
# global git options whose value is the NEXT argument: `git --namespace x push --force` still runs push
GIT_GLOBAL_VALUE_OPTIONS = ("-C", "-c", "--git-dir", "--work-tree", "--namespace", "--config-env", "--attr-source",
                            "--super-prefix")
# `git config` options that take a value as the next argument, with the shortest prefix git resolves to them
GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_OPTIONS = (("--file", 5), ("--blob", 4), ("--type", 3), ("--default", 3), ("--comment", 9),
                            ("--value", 7), ("--url", 5))
# listing options of `git branch` whose value may be the next argument, with the shortest prefix git resolves
BRANCH_VALUE_OPTIONS = (("--sort", 4), ("--format", 6), ("--contains", 5), ("--no-contains", 8), ("--merged", 4),
                        ("--no-merged", 7), ("--points-at", 3))
CI_SWITCH = "Switching the CI gate or the branch protection off is reserved for the human."
# options of `gh api` that take a value: the word after them is not the endpoint
GH_API_VALUE_OPTIONS = ("-X", "--method", "-f", "--raw-field", "-F", "--field", "-H", "--header", "--input", "-q",
                        "--jq", "-t", "--template", "--hostname", "-p", "--preview", "--cache")
GH_MERGE_MUTATION = re.compile(r"\b(?:mergePullRequest|enablePullRequestAutoMerge|mergeBranch|enqueuePullRequest)\s*\(")
GH_PROTECTION_MUTATION = re.compile(r"\b(?:create|update|delete)(?:BranchProtectionRule|RepositoryRuleset)\s*\(")
HOOK_RUNNING = {"commit", "push", "merge", "pull", "am", "rebase", "cherry-pick", "revert"}   # --no-verify skips their hooks
SHELLS = {"bash", "sh", "zsh", "dash", "ksh", "mksh", "ash"}                # `-c` may sit in a cluster: bash -lc '...'
INTERPRETERS = {"python", "python3", "node", "ruby"} | SHELLS              # with -c / -e inline code
SHELL_LONG_VALUE_OPTIONS = ("--rcfile", "--init-file")
WRAPPERS = {"sudo", "command", "exec", "nohup", "time", "env", "timeout", "nice", "setsid", "stdbuf", "xargs"}
# options of wrappers that take a separate value: skipped together with the value so the wrapped command surfaces
WRAPPER_VALUE_OPTS = {
    "sudo": {"-u", "-g", "-p", "-r", "-t", "-C", "-U", "-h", "--user", "--group", "--prompt", "--role",
             "--type", "--close-from", "--other-user", "--host"},
    "env": {"-u", "-C", "-S", "--unset", "--chdir", "--split-string"},
    "exec": {"-a", "--argv0"},
    "time": {"-o", "-f", "--output", "--format"},
    "command": set(), "nohup": set(), "setsid": set(),
    "timeout": {"-s", "--signal", "-k", "--kill-after"},
    "nice": {"-n", "--adjustment"},
    "stdbuf": {"-i", "-o", "-e", "--input", "--output", "--error"},
    "xargs": {"-n", "-P", "-L", "-I", "-d", "-E", "-s", "-a", "--max-args", "--max-procs", "--max-lines",
              "--delimiter", "--eof", "--max-chars", "--arg-file", "--process-slot-var"},
}
SHELL_KEYWORDS = {"if", "then", "else", "elif", "do", "while", "until", "!", "{"}   # `then rm x` runs rm
GRADLE = {"gradlew", "gradle"}
GRADLE_PATH_OPTIONS = {"-p", "--project-dir", "-g", "--gradle-user-home", "--project-cache-dir", "-b", "--build-file",
                       "-c", "--settings-file", "-I", "--init-script", "--include-build"}
PERL_WRITES = re.compile(r"\b(open|unlink|rename|system|exec|qx|readpipe|mkdir|rmdir|truncate|chmod|chown|symlink|"
                         r"link|utime|syswrite|sysopen)\b|`")
# a perl switch cluster that ends in -e / -E: the program is the rest of the word or the next word (-ne, -lane, -0777ne)
PERL_PROGRAM_SWITCH = re.compile(r"(-[acdnpsStTuUwWXl0-9]*[eE])(.*)", re.S)
# -i edits in place (-pi, -i.bak, -wpi, a lone -i anywhere); M m I F C D V e E take the rest of their word, so the i
# of -Mstrict, -I/usr/lib or of an attached program (-neprint if ...) is none
PERL_IN_PLACE = re.compile(r"-(?!-)[^MmIFCDVeE]*i")
PERL_QUOTE_LIKE = {"q", "qq", "qw", "qx", "m", "qr", "s", "tr", "y"}
# perl expects a term after these, so a / that follows them opens a pattern (checked against perl 5.38)
PERL_BEFORE_PATTERN = {"", "(", ",", "!", "&&", "||", "=~", "!~", "{", ";", "if", "unless", "and", "or", "not",
                       "split", "grep", "for", "foreach", "while", "until"}
PERL_BRACKETS = {"(": ")", "[": "]", "{": "}", "<": ">"}
PERL_WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*(?:::\w+)*")
PERL_NUMBER = re.compile(r"\d[\d_]*(?:\.[\d_]+)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?")
PERL_VARIABLE = re.compile(r"\$(?:#?[A-Za-z_]\w*(?:::\w+)*|\d+|[&.,;!@/\\+-])|@(?:[A-Za-z_]\w*(?:::\w+)*|[-+])")
PERL_OPERATOR = re.compile(r"&&|\|\||=~|!~|==|!=|>=|=>|->|\.\.\.?|\+\+|--|\*\*|::|[-+*/%&.=!~^|\\(){}\[\],;:>]")
PERL_FLAGS = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]*")                  # the modifiers after a pattern or a quote-like text
PERL_READLINE = re.compile(r"<\$?\w*>")                # <>, <STDIN>, <$fh>
# what interpolating a pattern can run: (?{ }), (??{ }), (*{ }), @{[ ]}, ${\ }, $x{...}, $x[...]; a $ before ), | or
# the end is an anchor
PERL_PATTERN_CODE = re.compile(r"\(\s*[?*]\s*\??\s*\{|@|\$(?![)|]|\Z)")
# a redirection that writes a file: > >> >| &> &>>, <> (opens it for writing too) and >& - whose word may also be a
# file descriptor (`>&2` duplicates one, `>&-` closes it, `>&log` writes the file log)
REDIRECT = re.compile(r"(?<![<>])(<>|>&|>>?\|?)")
FD_WORD = re.compile(r"\d+-?|-")
# the descriptor written right before >& (`2>&word`, `{fd}>&word`): bash duplicates the word into it, and a word that is
# no number is an error there ("ambiguous redirect"), not a file. Only `>&word` and `1>&word` write the file `word`.
DUP_FD = re.compile(r"(?:^|(?<=[\s;&|(){}]))(\d+|\{[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\})$")
# A command the guard cannot read in time or at all is refused, not let through: a hook that crashes or exceeds
# Claude Code's timeout lets the command run. 300 nested $( ... ) took a minute to read and 1000 overflowed the stack;
# a command written by hand nests a few levels, and 32 are read in a fraction of a second.
MAX_NESTING = 32
JUDGE_SECONDS = 20
TOO_COMPLEX = ("The guard cannot judge this command ({}). Write it as several simpler commands; if this is "
               "really needed, ask the human.")
GLOB_CHARS = re.compile(r"[*?\[]")
STATEMENT_END = re.compile(r";|&&|\|\||\n")


def main():
    if os.environ.get("GAUNTLET_GUARD", "").lower() == "off":
        return 0
    try:
        event = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except Exception:
        return 0
    project = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR") or event.get("cwd") or os.getcwd()
    agent = event.get("agent_type") or "main"
    tool = event.get("tool_name", "")
    params = event.get("tool_input") or {}
    ctx = Context(project)
    if tool in ("Edit", "Write", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"):
        path = params.get("file_path") or params.get("notebook_path") or ""
        reason = (user_config_reason(path, (project, event.get("cwd")))
                  or path_violation(agent, ctx.relative(path), ctx))
    elif tool == "Bash":
        reason = bash_violation(agent, params.get("command", ""), ctx, event.get("cwd") or project)
    else:
        reason = None
    if reason:
        print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
            "permissionDecision": "deny",
            "permissionDecisionReason": "[gauntlet guard] " + reason}}))
    return 0


class JudgeTimeout(BaseException):
    """The reading ran out of time. A BaseException, so that no `except Exception` on the way swallows it."""


def nesting_depth(command):
    """How deep $( ... ), <( ... ) and >( ... ) nest, counted on the raw text without regard to quotes. It refuses an
    absurd command early; what it miscounts is caught by the time budget and the recursion limit in bash_violation."""
    depth = deepest = 0
    for i, c in enumerate(command):
        if c == "(" and i and command[i - 1] in "$<>":
            depth += 1
            deepest = max(deepest, depth)
        elif c == ")" and depth:
            depth -= 1
    return deepest


def bash_violation(agent, command, ctx, cwd):
    """command_violation, refused instead of crashing or running out of time."""
    depth = nesting_depth(command)
    if depth > MAX_NESTING:
        return TOO_COMPLEX.format(f"$( ... ) nested {depth} levels deep")
    timer = hasattr(signal, "SIGALRM")
    if timer:
        def expired(signum, frame):
            raise JudgeTimeout
        previous = signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, expired)
        signal.alarm(JUDGE_SECONDS)
    try:
        return command_violation(agent, command, ctx, cwd)
    except RecursionError:
        return TOO_COMPLEX.format("it nests too deeply to read")
    except JudgeTimeout:
        return TOO_COMPLEX.format(f"reading it took longer than {JUDGE_SECONDS} s")
    finally:
        if timer:
            signal.alarm(0)
            signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, previous)


def features_rel_of(value):
    """acceptance.features as gauntlet.gradle reads it: an empty value is the default, and "./src/.../features/"
    names the directory "src/.../features" - as a text prefix it named no path, and the spec was not frozen."""
    value = (value or "").strip() or DEFAULT_FEATURES
    return os.path.normpath(value).replace(os.sep, "/").strip("/")


def module_dirs_of(value):
    """module as CI reads it: comma-separated build directories, every entry stripped of blanks and slashes and
    read as a path - ./core, core/. and core/ are core, . and ./ the build at the repository root. As a text
    prefix ./core named no path: the main agent could write the module's spec, the specifier and hardener nothing."""
    dirs = []
    for entry in (value or "").split(","):
        d = os.path.normpath(entry.strip()).replace(os.sep, "/").strip("/") if entry.strip() else ""
        if d and d not in dirs:
            dirs.append(d)
    return [] if dirs == ["."] else dirs


class Context:
    """Where the specification lives, which branch is the base, and whether the spec is frozen."""

    def __init__(self, project):
        self.project = project
        props = read_properties(os.path.join(project, PROPERTIES))
        # module = the Gradle build directories inside a monorepo, comma-separated ("" = the repository root)
        self.modules = module_dirs_of(props.get("module"))
        prefixes = ["" if m == "." else m + "/" for m in self.modules] or [""]
        features_rel = features_rel_of(props.get("acceptance.features")) + "/"
        self.features_dirs = tuple(pfx + features_rel for pfx in prefixes)
        self.test_code = tuple(pfx + p for pfx in prefixes for p in TEST_CODE)
        self.src_main = [pfx + "src/main" for pfx in prefixes]
        self.build_dirs = tuple(pfx + d for pfx in prefixes for d in ("build/", ".gradle/")) + ("build/", ".gradle/")
        self.base_ref = props.get("baseRef", DEFAULT_BASE)
        self.base_branch = self.base_ref.split("/", 1)[1] if "/" in self.base_ref else self.base_ref
        self.approval = props.get("spec.approval", "chat").lower()
        self._frozen = None
        self._worktrees = None

    @property
    def frozen(self):
        """True once the branch holds a commit that touches the feature files and they differ from the
        base branch: the human approved the specification in the chat and the agent committed it. From
        then on only the human changes it. Once the base branch has the same feature files (the PR was
        merged) the branch is free again. Fails open (not frozen) when the base branch cannot be found."""
        if self._frozen is None:
            if self.approval == "pr":
                self._frozen = False    # spec.approval=pr: the human reads the spec in the PR, no freeze
            elif git_code(self.project, "symbolic-ref", "-q", "HEAD") != 0:
                self._frozen = True     # detached HEAD: not the task's branch, nothing may be specified here
            else:
                specs = [d.rstrip("/") for d in self.features_dirs]   # one task per branch: any module's spec freezes all
                count = git(self.project, "rev-list", "--count", f"{self.base_ref}..HEAD", "--", *specs)
                differs = git_code(self.project, "diff", "--quiet", self.base_ref, "HEAD", "--", *specs) == 1
                self._frozen = count.isdigit() and int(count) > 0 and differs
        return self._frozen

    def relative(self, path, cwd=None):
        """The path relative to the project - or, for a file in ANOTHER worktree of the same repository
        (`git worktree add ../wt`), relative to that worktree: its gauntlet/, .claude/ and feature files are the
        same human-owned files in another checkout, and a commit made there lands in the same repository."""
        rel = relative(path, self.project, cwd)
        if rel is not None or not path:
            return rel
        if self._worktrees is None:
            listing = git(self.project, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
            self._worktrees = [os.path.realpath(line[len("worktree "):]) for line in listing.splitlines()
                               if line.startswith("worktree ")]
        for root in self._worktrees:
            rel = relative(path, root, cwd)
            if rel is not None:
                return rel
        return None

    def role_scope(self, agent):
        """Where a role may write: () is read-only - the reviewer and the checker, the subagent that runs the
        read-only cards of the core (code maps, framework checks, the critic, refuters); None is no role."""
        return {"specifier": self.features_dirs, "hardener": self.test_code, "reviewer": (), "checker": ()}.get(agent)

    def protected(self, agent):
        paths = [p.rstrip("/") for p in HUMAN_OWNED]
        if agent != "specifier" or self.frozen:
            paths += [d.rstrip("/") for d in self.features_dirs]
        if agent == "hardener":
            paths += self.src_main
        return paths

    def is_spec(self, path):
        return path in [d.rstrip("/") for d in self.features_dirs]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- paths

def relative(path, project, cwd=None):
    if not path:
        return None
    base = cwd or project
    absolute = os.path.realpath(path if os.path.isabs(path) else os.path.join(base, path))
    rel = os.path.relpath(absolute, os.path.realpath(project)).replace(os.sep, "/")
    return None if rel.startswith("..") else rel


def is_under(rel, prefixes):
    r = rel.lower()
    return any(r == p.rstrip("/").lower() or r.startswith((p if p.endswith("/") else p + "/").lower()) for p in prefixes)


def contains(rel, prefixes):
    """The path is a parent of a protected path (rm -rf src takes the features with it)."""
    if rel == ".":
        return True
    r = rel.lower()
    return any(p.rstrip("/").lower().startswith(r + "/") for p in prefixes)


# The user's agent configuration outside the repository: settings, hooks, rules, instructions, agents and skills that
# an agent tool loads for every project. Whoever writes there can switch the hooks off for the next session or rewrite
# what an agent reads as its instructions. Each entry: the place - "~/..." or "/etc/...", or "$NAME" for the place an
# environment variable moves it to (the guard sees the environment Claude Code started with) -, whose it is, why it
# matters, and the subdirectories that are the tool's own session data: Kimi Code and Grok Build keep their sessions
# under their home and their agent writes its plan file there, and Grok Build runs a worktree session under
# worktrees/ (gauntlet/adapters/kimi.md, grok.md). The place itself and everything under it count, in any letter case.
SWITCH = "it could switch the hooks off"
USER_CONFIG = (
    ("~/.claude", "the user's Claude Code configuration", SWITCH, ()),
    ("~/.codex", "the user's Codex configuration", SWITCH, ()),
    ("$CODEX_HOME", "the user's Codex configuration", SWITCH, ()),
    ("/etc/codex", "the machine's Codex configuration", SWITCH, ()),
    ("~/.gemini", "the user's Gemini CLI and Antigravity configuration", SWITCH, ()),
    ("~/.agents", "the user's instructions, agents and skills of Codex, Antigravity and Kimi Code",
     "every session of theirs loads them", ()),
    ("~/.grok", "the user's Grok Build configuration", SWITCH, ("sessions", "worktrees")),
    ("$GROK_HOME", "the user's Grok Build configuration", SWITCH, ("sessions", "worktrees")),
    ("/etc/grok", "the machine's Grok Build configuration", SWITCH, ()),
    ("~/.kimi-code", "the user's Kimi Code configuration", SWITCH, ("sessions",)),
    ("$KIMI_CODE_HOME", "the user's Kimi Code configuration", SWITCH, ("sessions",)),
    ("~/.qwen", "the user's Qwen Code configuration", SWITCH, ()),
    ("$QWEN_HOME", "the user's Qwen Code configuration", SWITCH, ()),
