    cmd, args = os.path.basename(words[0]), words[1:]
    if cmd == "tar":                                      # listing, comparing and writing to stdout change nothing
        return archive_mode(args) not in ("t", "d") and bool(archive_targets(args))
    if cmd == "unzip":                                    # -l -v -Z list, -t tests, -p prints to stdout, -z the comment
        return not any(a.startswith("-") and set(a[1:]) & set("lvZtpz") for a in args)
    if cmd in MUTATING_COMMANDS:
        return True
    if cmd == "sed":
        return "i" in short_flags(args) or "--in-place" in args
    if cmd == "perl":                      # code comes with -e / -E, -M / -m ('-MPOSIX;rmdir(...)') and -F (a pattern)
        return any(PERL_IN_PLACE.match(a) for a in args) or (bool(set(short_flags(args)) & set("eEMmF"))
                                                             and perl_writes(raw if raw is not None else segment))
    if cmd in ("awk", "gawk"):
        return "-i" in args or any(a.startswith("-i") for a in args)
    if cmd in SHELLS:
        return False                       # its -c payload is a command line of its own: see nested_violation
    if is_interpreter(cmd):
        return inline_code(words)
    if cmd == "git":
        index = git_subcommand_index(args)
        sub, rest = (args[index], args[index + 1:]) if index >= 0 else ("", [])
        if sub not in GIT_WORKTREE_WRITING or git_read_only(sub, rest):
            return False
        if sub == "restore":               # --staged without --worktree only takes changes out of the index
            staged = any(a in ("--staged", "-S") for a in rest)
            return not staged or any(a in ("--worktree", "-W") for a in rest)
        if sub == "reset":                 # only --hard, --merge and --keep touch the files
            return any(a in ("--hard", "--merge", "--keep") for a in rest)
        return True
    if cmd == "find":                      # it writes when it deletes, prints to a file or runs a command that writes
        if any(a in ("-delete", "-fprint", "-fprint0", "-fls", "-fprintf") for a in args):
            return True
        return any(writes_worktree(words_of(code), code) for code in inline_code_strings(cmd, args))
    return False


def perl_writes(text):
    """True when the perl command line `text` (as written) names a call that writes, in its program or in its other
    words (-M'POSIX;system(...)' is code too). The program is the one perl runs: the -e / -E texts, separate or
    attached (-esystem(...)), joined by newlines. Its match patterns are data - `perl -ne 'print if /`/'` and
    `perl -ne 'print if /open/'` only read."""
    try:
        words = shlex.split(text, posix=True)
    except ValueError:
        words = []
    start = next((k for k, w in enumerate(words) if os.path.basename(w) == "perl"), None)
    if start is None:
        return bool(PERL_WRITES.search(text))
    other, programs, i = words[:start + 1], [], start + 1
    while i < len(words):
        switch = PERL_PROGRAM_SWITCH.fullmatch(words[i])
        if switch and (switch.group(2) or i + 1 < len(words)):
            programs.append(switch.group(2) or words[i + 1])
            i += 1 if switch.group(2) else 2
        elif words[i].startswith("-") and words[i] not in ("-", "--"):
            other.append(words[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            other += words[i:]              # the script or the first file: perl reads no more switches
            break
    return bool(PERL_WRITES.search(" ".join(other)) or PERL_WRITES.search(perl_without_patterns("\n".join(programs))))


def perl_without_patterns(code):
    """perl's program without the text of its match patterns: a pattern is data, `print if /`/` and `s/system//`
    call nothing. Only what perl certainly reads as a pattern goes - a / where perl expects a term (see
    PERL_BEFORE_PATTERN), the pattern of m// and of s/// - and only when it runs no code (PERL_PATTERN_CODE).
    Strings, qr//, tr/// and the replacement of s/// (code with /e) stay. Whatever this reader does not follow
    exactly leaves the whole program as it is: a comment, ?, POD, a heredoc or <...> glob, ${...}, $$, $', a
    quote-like word after a sigil, -> or - (&s, ->s, -s, %m), a / after a variable (perl reads
    `print $fh /.../` as a pattern), after a word or after a }."""
    out, prev, i = [], "", 0
    while i < len(code):
        c = code[i]
        if c.isspace():
            out.append(c)
            i += 1
            continue
        if c in "#?" or (c == "=" and (i == 0 or code[i - 1] == "\n")):
            return code                                  # a comment, ?PATTERN?, POD
        word = PERL_WORD.match(code, i)
        if word:
            name, end = word.group(0), word.end()
            if name in ("sub", "format", "__END__", "__DATA__") or code.startswith("'", end):
                return code                              # a sub's name, a format, data, Foo'bar
            sigil = prev in ("%", "&", "*", "-", "->", "::")     # &s, %m, -s, ->s: a name, not an operator
            if name in PERL_QUOTE_LIKE:
                read = perl_quote_like(code, end, name)
                if read is None or sigil or prev in ("package", "use", "no", "require"):
                    return code                          # a name (use s, ->s), =>, $h{s}, a text never closed
                spans, end = read
                out.append(perl_pattern(code, i, end, spans[0]) if name in ("m", "s") else code[i:end])
                prev, i = "term", end
                continue
            out.append(name)
            prev, i = ("name" if sigil else name), end
            continue
        if c == "/" and prev in PERL_BEFORE_PATTERN:
            close = perl_closing(code, i)
            if close < 0:
                return code
            end = PERL_FLAGS.match(code, close + 1).end()
            out.append(perl_pattern(code, i, end, (i + 1, close)))
            prev, i = "term", end
            continue
        if c in "'\"`":
            close = perl_closing(code, i)
            if close < 0:
                return code
            out.append(code[i:close + 1])
            prev, i = "term", close + 1
            continue
        if c == "<":
            readline = PERL_READLINE.match(code, i)
            if not readline or prev not in PERL_BEFORE_PATTERN:
                return code                              # a heredoc, a glob, a comparison
            out.append(readline.group(0))
            prev, i = "term", readline.end()
            continue
        token = PERL_NUMBER.match(code, i) or PERL_VARIABLE.match(code, i) or PERL_OPERATOR.match(code, i)
        if not token or (c == "/" and prev != "term") or (c == "{" and prev in ("%", "&", "*")):
            return code                                  # a / after a variable or a word may open a pattern
        out.append(token.group(0))
        prev = ("term" if c.isdigit() or c in ")]" else "variable" if c in "$@" else token.group(0))
        i = token.end()
    return "".join(out)


def perl_quote_like(code, i, word):
    """([(start, end) of each delimited text], the end of the construct) of perl's quote-like `word` whose
    delimiters start at i - or None when it is not read exactly: =>, a hash key ($h{s}), a comment or a letter for a
    delimiter, a text that is never closed."""
    spans, k = [], i
    for part in range(2 if word in ("s", "tr", "y") else 1):
        if part == 0 or code[k] in "}])>":              # s{...}{...}: the replacement has delimiters of its own
            k += part
            while k < len(code) and code[k].isspace():
                k += 1
            if (k == len(code) or code[k] in "=)]}>:\\" or code[k] == "_" or code[k].isalnum()
                    or (code[k] == "#" and (part or k > i))):
                return None
        close = perl_closing(code, k)
        if close < 0:
            return None
        spans.append((k + 1, close))
        k = close                                        # s/.../.../: the middle delimiter is shared
    return spans, PERL_FLAGS.match(code, k + 1).end()


def perl_closing(code, i):
    """Index of the delimiter that closes the one at i, or -1: a bracket nests, any other character closes at its
    next unescaped occurrence."""
    opening = code[i]
    closing, depth, k = PERL_BRACKETS.get(opening, opening), 0, i + 1
    while k < len(code):
        if code[k] == "\\":
            k += 1
        elif code[k] == closing:
            if depth == 0:
                return k
            depth -= 1
        elif code[k] == opening:
            depth += 1
        k += 1
    return -1


def perl_pattern(code, start, end, span):
    """code[start:end] without the text of the pattern at span - unless interpolating that pattern can run code."""
    if PERL_PATTERN_CODE.search(re.sub(r"\\.", "", code[span[0]:span[1]], flags=re.S)):
        return code[start:end]
    return code[start:span[0]] + code[span[1]:end]


def changes_state(words, segment, cwd=None, ctx=None, raw=None):
    if words and os.path.basename(words[0]) == "git":
        sub = git_subcommand(words[1:])
        rest = words[words.index(sub) + 1:] if sub in words else []
        return sub in GIT_STATE_CHANGING and not git_read_only(sub, rest)
    if not writes_worktree(words, segment, raw):
        return False
    if ctx is not None and os.path.basename(words[0]) in MUTATING_COMMANDS:
        tokens = path_tokens(words, cwd, ctx.project)
        if tokens and all(ctx.relative(expand(t, cwd, ctx.project), c) is None
                          for t in tokens for c in candidates(cwd, ctx.project)):
            return False                   # everything it touches lies outside the project: tee /tmp/x.log, mkdir /tmp/review
    return True


def git_read_only(sub, rest):
    """`git branch -a`, `git stash list`, `git tag -l 'v*'`, `git tag --contains HEAD`: listing forms of otherwise
    state-changing commands. A word that is no option makes `git branch` and `git tag` create something - unless
    it is the value of a listing option or a pattern after -l / --list."""
    forms = GIT_READ_ONLY_FORMS.get(sub)
    if forms is None:
        return False
    if not rest:
        return sub != "stash"              # bare `git stash` saves; bare branch/tag/notes/submodule list
    if sub in ("stash", "worktree", "notes", "submodule"):
        return rest[0] in forms
    args = branch_options(rest)            # without the values of --sort, --format, --contains, --merged, ...
    listing = any(a in ("-l", "--list") for a in args)
    for a in args:
        if a.startswith("--"):
            ok = a.split("=", 1)[0] in forms
        elif a.startswith("-") and len(a) > 1:
            ok = set(a[1:]) <= set("larvi") or (sub == "tag" and re.fullmatch(r"-n\d*", a) is not None)
        else:
            ok = listing                   # a pattern
        if not ok:
            return False
    return True


def git_subcommand_index(args):
    """Index of the subcommand in a git argument list, or -1. Global options are skipped together with the
    value of those that take it as the next argument: `git --namespace x commit --amend` is a commit."""
    skip = False
    for i, a in enumerate(args):
        if skip:
            skip = False
        elif a in GIT_GLOBAL_VALUE_OPTIONS:
            skip = True
        elif not a.startswith("-"):
            return i
    return -1


def git_subcommand(args):
    index = git_subcommand_index(args)
    return args[index] if index >= 0 else ""


def sed_files(args):
    """The file operands of sed. Its script - the first operand, unless -e or -f gives it - is not a path,
    although `s/a/b/` looks like one."""
    files, script, i = [], False, 0
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if a.startswith("--"):
            script = script or a.split("=", 1)[0] in ("--expression", "--file")
            i += 1 if "=" in a or a.split("=", 1)[0] not in ("--expression", "--file") else 2
        elif a.startswith("-") and len(a) > 1:
            flags = a[1:]
            if not flags.startswith("i") and ("e" in flags or "f" in flags):   # -i.bak is a suffix, not flags
                script = True
                i += 1 if flags[-1] not in "ef" else 2      # -e SCRIPT / -ne SCRIPT: the script is the next word
            else:
                i += 1
        elif not script:
            script = True
            i += 1
        else:
            files.append(a)
            i += 1
    return files


def awk_files(args):
    """The file operands of awk: the program (the first operand, unless -f gives it) is not a path."""
    files, program, i = [], False, 0
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if a in ("-f", "--file", "-v", "--assign", "-F", "--field-separator", "-i", "--include"):
            program = program or a in ("-f", "--file")
            i += 2
        elif a.startswith("-") and len(a) > 1:
            program = program or a.startswith(("-f", "--file="))
            i += 1
        elif not program:
            program = True
            i += 1
        else:
            files.append(a)
            i += 1
    return files


def find_roots(args):
    """Where find searches (`.` when nothing is named) and the files its -fprint actions write. The tests of
    its expression (`-name '*.java'`) are not paths, and the command of -exec is judged as a command."""
    roots, i = [], 0
    while i < len(args) and args[i] in ("-H", "-L", "-P"):
        i += 1
    while i < len(args) and not args[i].startswith("-") and args[i] not in ("(", ")", "!", ","):
        roots.append(args[i])
        i += 1
    written = [args[k + 1] for k in range(i, len(args) - 1) if args[k] in ("-fprint", "-fprint0", "-fls", "-fprintf")]
    return (roots or ["."]) + written


def copy_destination(args):
    """What cp / install / rsync / ln write: the last operand, or the directory of -t / --target-directory. The
    sources are only read - copying a config out of the project changes nothing in it."""
    operands, target, skip = [], None, False
    for i, a in enumerate(args):
        if skip:
            skip = False
        elif a in ("-t", "--target-directory"):
            target, skip = (args[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(args) else None), True
        elif a.startswith("--target-directory="):
            target = a.split("=", 1)[1]
        elif not a.startswith("-") or a == "-":
            operands.append(a)
    return [target] if target else operands[-1:]


def archive_targets(args):
    """What tar writes: the archive when it creates or appends; when it extracts, the directory of -C (or the
    current one) - or the members named after the archive within it. The archive it reads is no target."""
    archive, base, operands, skip = None, None, [], False
    for k, a in enumerate(args):
        following = args[k + 1] if k + 1 < len(args) else None
        if skip:
            skip = False
        elif a.startswith("--file="):
            archive = a.split("=", 1)[1]
        elif a.startswith("--directory="):
            base = a.split("=", 1)[1]
        elif a in ("--file", "--directory", "-C"):
            archive, base, skip = (following if a == "--file" else archive), (base if a == "--file" else following), True
        elif (k == 0 or a.startswith("-")) and not a.startswith("--") and a.endswith("f"):
            archive, skip = following, True     # the archive follows a bundle of flags that ends in f
        elif not a.startswith("-") and k > 0:
            operands.append(a)
    if archive_mode(args) in ("c", "r", "u", "A"):
        return [archive] if archive and archive != "-" else []
    return [os.path.join(base or ".", member) for member in operands] or [base or "."]


def unzip_targets(args):
    """Where unzip extracts: the directory of -d, or the current one. The archive is only read."""
    for k, a in enumerate(args):
        if a == "-d" and k + 1 < len(args):
            return [args[k + 1]]
        if a.startswith("-d") and len(a) > 2:
            return [a[2:]]
    return ["."]


OPERANDS = {"sed": sed_files, "awk": awk_files, "gawk": awk_files, "find": find_roots, "tar": archive_targets,
            "unzip": unzip_targets, "cp": copy_destination, "install": copy_destination, "rsync": copy_destination,
            "ln": copy_destination}
# a word that is a directory the hook knows (expand): `rm -rf "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"` and `rm -rf $PWD` name the project
KNOWN_DIRECTORY = re.compile(r"\$(?:CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR|PWD|\{CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\}|\{PWD\})")


def path_tokens(words, cwd, project):
    """Path-like arguments of a command, with `git -C dir` honoured and globs expanded."""
    if not words:
        return []
    cmd, args = os.path.basename(words[0]), words[1:]
    base = cwd
    if cmd in OPERANDS:
        args = OPERANDS[cmd](args)          # a sed script, an awk program and a find test are not paths
    if cmd == "git" and "-C" in args and args.index("-C") + 1 < len(args):
        target = args[args.index("-C") + 1]
        base = os.path.realpath(target if os.path.isabs(target) else os.path.join(cwd, target))
    tokens = []
    for a in args:
        if a.startswith("-") and not a.startswith("-/"):
            continue
        if GLOB_CHARS.search(a):
            pattern = a if os.path.isabs(a) else os.path.join(base, a)
            tokens.extend(glob.glob(pattern) or [a])
        elif "/" in a or a in (".", "..") or KNOWN_DIRECTORY.fullmatch(a) or os.path.exists(os.path.join(base, a)):
            tokens.append(a)
    if base == cwd:
        return tokens
    return [t if os.path.isabs(t) else os.path.join(base, t) for t in tokens]   # git -C dir: resolve against dir


def written_words(words):
    """The operands a writing command may write - the written ones of sed, cp, tar, ... (OPERANDS), every other
    command's all - also a name that does not exist yet, which path_tokens leaves out."""
    if not words:
        return []
    cmd, args = os.path.basename(words[0]), words[1:]
    if cmd == "dd":
        return [a[3:] for a in args if a.startswith("of=")]      # it writes the file of of=, reads the one of if=
    if cmd in OPERANDS:
        args = OPERANDS[cmd](args)
    return [a for a in args if a and not a.startswith("-")]


def unseen(words, cwd):
    """The written operands path_tokens leaves out: a bare name that does not exist yet (`mv /tmp/x AGENTS.md`) and
    the file of dd's of=, which it takes for a name that starts with `of=` - their statement is matched as text."""
    dd = bool(words) and os.path.basename(words[0]) == "dd"
    return [w for w in written_words(words) if dd or ("/" not in w and w not in (".", "..") and not GLOB_CHARS.search(w)
                                                      and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(str(cwd), w)))]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers

PROPERTY = re.compile(r"([^=:\s]+)\s*[=:]?\s*(.*)$")


def read_properties(path):
    """The settings of gauntlet.properties with the separators java.util.Properties reads (gauntlet.gradle loads
    the same file with it): `key=value`, `key: value` and `key value`; `#` and `!` start a comment line."""
    props = {}
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for line in f:
                m = PROPERTY.match(line.strip())
                if m and line.strip()[0] not in "#!":
                    props[m.group(1)] = m.group(2).strip()
    except OSError:
        pass
    return props


def git(project, *args):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", project, "-c", "core.quotePath=false", *args], stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                              stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, timeout=30).stdout.strip()
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return ""


def git_code(project, *args):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", project, *args], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                              timeout=30).returncode
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return -1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===== BEGIN FILE gauntlet/hooks/selftest.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Self-test for the gauntlet hooks. Builds a throwaway git repository with a fake base branch and
runs guard.py / stop_gate.py against it the way Claude Code does (JSON on stdin, environment set).

    python3 gauntlet/hooks/selftest.py          # from any directory; needs git and python3

Gradle is stubbed with a fake ./gradlew that exits with the code found in a marker file, so the
Stop-gate logic is exercised without a JVM.
"""
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

HOOKS = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
KIT = os.path.dirname(HOOKS)
FEATURES_REL = "src/acceptanceTest/resources/features"
MODULES = []          # Gradle builds inside the repository: [] = one build at the root, ["core", "adapter"] = monorepo
M = ""                # prefix of the module the shared tests work in ("" or "core/")
FEATURES = FEATURES_REL


def gate_tasks():
    """What the Stop hook demands a "> Task" line for after a green exit (stop_gate.GATE_TASKS), by task."""
    import importlib.util
    saved, sys.dont_write_bytecode = sys.dont_write_bytecode, True      # the kit stays as it is
    try:
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("sg_tasks", os.path.join(HOOKS, "stop_gate.py"))
        sg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(sg)
    finally:
        sys.dont_write_bytecode = saved
    return {task: sg.gate_tasks(task) for task in sg.GATE_TASKS}


# Green, it names every task it ran the way Gradle does with --console=plain: "> Task :<name>"
FAKE_GRADLEW = ("#!/bin/sh\ncode=$(cat build/gauntlet/fake-exit 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\n"
                "echo \"fake gradle $*\"\n"
                "if [ \"$code\" = 0 ]; then\n  case $1 in\n"
                + "".join(f"    {task}) names='{' '.join(names)}' ;;\n" for task, names in gate_tasks().items())
                + "    *) names=$1 ;;\n  esac\n  for n in $names; do echo \"> Task :$n\"; done\n"
                "else\n  echo 'CRAP FAIL com.example.X#y'\nfi\nexit $code\n")
failures = []
passed = 0


def sh(repo, *cmd, **kw):
    return subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=repo, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, **kw)


def git(repo, *args):
    r = sh(repo, "git", *args)
    assert r.returncode == 0, f"git {' '.join(args)}: {r.stdout}"
    return r.stdout.strip()


def make_repo():
    root = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="gauntlet-selftest-")
    repo = os.path.join(root, "service")
    bare = os.path.join(root, "origin.git")
    os.makedirs(repo)
    git(repo, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
    git(repo, "config", "user.email", "t@example.com")
    git(repo, "config", "user.name", "t")
    shutil.copytree(KIT, os.path.join(repo, "gauntlet"), ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__"))
    # the layout under test decides `module`, not the installed kit's value (a monorepo install sets it)
    props = os.path.join(repo, "gauntlet/config/gauntlet.properties")
    with open(props) as f:
        lines = [line for line in f.read().splitlines() if not line.strip().startswith("module=")]
    with open(props, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines) + f"\nmodule={','.join(MODULES)}\n")
    for prefix in [m + "/" for m in MODULES] or [""]:
        write(repo, prefix + "build.gradle.kts", 'plugins { java }\napply(from = "../gauntlet/gauntlet.gradle")\n')
        write(repo, prefix + "src/main/java/com/example/service/domain/Order.java",
              "package com.example.service.domain;\npublic class Order { public int discount(int p) { return p / 10; } }\n")
        write(repo, prefix + "src/test/java/com/example/service/domain/OrderTest.java",
              "package com.example.service.domain;\nclass OrderTest { }\n")
        write(repo, prefix + FEATURES_REL + "/.gitkeep", "")
        write(repo, prefix + "gradlew", FAKE_GRADLEW)
        os.chmod(os.path.join(repo, prefix + "gradlew"), 0o755)
    git(repo, "add", "-A")
    git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "base")
    subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", "--bare", bare], check=True)
    git(repo, "remote", "add", "origin", bare)
    git(repo, "push", "-q", "origin", "main")
    git(repo, "checkout", "-q", "-b", "claude/feature-x")
    return repo


def write(repo, rel, text):
    path = os.path.join(repo, rel)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        f.write(text)


def run_hook(repo, script, event, env=None, args=()):
    e = dict(os.environ, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=repo)
    e.pop("GAUNTLET_GUARD", None)
    e.pop("GAUNTLET_STOP_HOOK", None)
    e.update(env or {})
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(repo, "gauntlet", "hooks", script), *args], cwd=repo,
                       input=json.dumps(event), stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, env=e)
    return r


def guard(repo, agent, tool, **params):
    event = {"session_id": "s1", "cwd": repo, "tool_name": tool, "tool_input": params}
    if agent != "main":
        event["agent_type"] = agent
    r = run_hook(repo, "guard.py", event)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return "CRASH " + r.stderr
    if not r.stdout.strip():
        return None
    return json.loads(r.stdout)["hookSpecificOutput"]["permissionDecisionReason"]


def check(name, condition, detail=""):
    global passed
    if condition:
        passed += 1
    else:
        failures.append(f"{name}  {detail}")


# The checker - the subagent that runs the read-only cards - has the reviewer's rights: every reviewer check runs for it too
TWINS = {"reviewer": ("checker",)}


def expect_deny(repo, name, agent, tool, **params):
    for who in (agent,) + TWINS.get(agent, ()):
        reason = guard(repo, who, tool, **params)
        check(name if who == agent else f"{name} [{who}]", reason is not None and not reason.startswith("CRASH"),
              f"expected deny, got {reason!r}")


def expect_allow(repo, name, agent, tool, **params):
    for who in (agent,) + TWINS.get(agent, ()):
        reason = guard(repo, who, tool, **params)
        check(name if who == agent else f"{name} [{who}]", reason is None, f"expected allow, got {reason!r}")


def guard_tests(repo):
    feature = FEATURES + "/order.feature"
    # --- human-owned files
    for path in ("gauntlet/config/gauntlet.properties", "gauntlet/gauntlet.gradle", "gauntlet/hooks/guard.py",
                 ".claude/settings.json", ".claude/agents/specifier.md", "CLAUDE.md", ".github/workflows/gauntlet.yml",
                 ".github/workflows/gauntlet-kit.yml"):
        expect_deny(repo, f"edit {path}", "main", "Edit", file_path=path, old_string="a", new_string="b")
    expect_deny(repo, "write absolute gauntlet path", "main", "Write",
                file_path=os.path.join(repo, "gauntlet/config/crap-allowlist.txt"), content="x")
    expect_allow(repo, "edit main code", "main", "Edit", file_path=M + "src/main/java/com/example/service/domain/Order.java",
                 old_string="a", new_string="b")
    expect_allow(repo, "edit build.gradle.kts", "main", "Edit", file_path=M + "build.gradle.kts", old_string="a", new_string="b")
    expect_allow(repo, "write step definitions", "main", "Write",
                 file_path=M + "src/acceptanceTest/java/com/example/service/acceptance/Steps.java", content="x")
    # --- shell writes to protected paths
    expect_deny(repo, "sed -i on gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command="sed -i 's/8/80/' gauntlet/config/gauntlet.properties")
    expect_deny(repo, "redirect into gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command="echo x > gauntlet/config/crap-allowlist.txt")
    expect_deny(repo, "cp over .claude", "main", "Bash", command="cp /tmp/s.json .claude/settings.json")
    expect_deny(repo, "python -c writing CLAUDE.md", "main", "Bash", command="python3 -c \"open('CLAUDE.md','w').write('')\"")
    expect_deny(repo, "git checkout gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command="git checkout -- gauntlet/config/checkstyle.xml")
    expect_deny(repo, "rm gauntlet dir", "main", "Bash", command="rm -rf gauntlet")
    expect_deny(repo, "rm the kit-files check of CI", "main", "Bash", command="rm .github/workflows/gauntlet-kit.yml")
    expect_deny(repo, "hook switch", "main", "Bash", command="GAUNTLET_GUARD=off ./gradlew gauntlet")
    expect_deny(repo, "export hook switch", "main", "Bash", command="export GAUNTLET_STOP_HOOK=off; ./gradlew test")
    # a command the guard cannot read is refused: a crashed or timed-out hook lets it run (review of 7061885)
    deep, hidden = "touch gauntlet/config/x", "touch gauntlet/config/x"
    for _ in range(100):
        deep = f"echo $({deep})"
    for _ in range(1000):
        hidden = f"echo ')' $({hidden})"      # the quoted ) defeats the nesting count; the reader overflows
    expect_deny(repo, "$( ... ) nested 100 levels deep", "main", "Bash", command=deep)
    expect_deny(repo, "$( ... ) nested 1000 levels deep behind quoted parentheses", "main", "Bash", command=hidden)
    shallow = "cat gauntlet/config/gauntlet.properties"
    for _ in range(10):
        shallow = f"echo $({shallow})"
    expect_allow(repo, "$( ... ) nested 10 levels deep that only reads", "main", "Bash", command=shallow)
    # --- no false positives
    expect_allow(repo, "gradlew gauntletFast", "main", "Bash", command="./gradlew gauntletFast --continue")
    expect_allow(repo, "gradlew gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command="./gradlew gauntlet --continue -Pgauntlet.baseRef=origin/main")
    expect_allow(repo, "cat gauntlet file", "main", "Bash", command="cat gauntlet/config/gauntlet.properties")
    expect_allow(repo, "git add -A", "main", "Bash", command="git add -A && git commit -m 'feat: discount'")
    expect_allow(repo, "git add gauntlet path", "main", "Bash", command="git add gauntlet/ .claude/ CLAUDE.md")
    expect_allow(repo, "commit mentioning gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command='git commit -m "chore: install the gauntlet"')
    expect_allow(repo, "git push own branch", "main", "Bash", command="git push -u origin HEAD")
    expect_allow(repo, "git push named branch", "main", "Bash", command="git push origin claude/feature-x")
    expect_allow(repo, "rm build/reports", "main", "Bash", command=f"rm -rf {M}build/reports")
    expect_allow(repo, "rm build/gauntlet (hook log dir)", "main", "Bash", command=f"rm -rf {M}build/gauntlet")
    expect_allow(repo, "tee into build/gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command=f"./gradlew gauntletFast 2>&1 | tee {M}build/gauntlet/run.log")
    expect_allow(repo, "cp hook log out", "main", "Bash", command=f"cp {M}build/gauntlet/gauntletFast-hook.log /tmp/")
    expect_allow(repo, "stash with gauntlet in message", "main", "Bash", command='git stash push -m "before gauntlet run"')
    expect_allow(repo, "mkdir build dir", "main", "Bash", command=f"mkdir -p {M}build/tmp && echo x > {M}build/tmp/a.txt")
    expect_allow(repo, "redirect 2>&1", "main", "Bash", command="./gradlew test 2>&1 | tail -20")
    expect_allow(repo, "redirect to /dev/null", "main", "Bash", command="./gradlew test > /dev/null 2>&1")
    expect_deny(repo, "quoted redirect into gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command='echo x > "gauntlet/config/crap-allowlist.txt"')
    expect_deny(repo, "heredoc into CLAUDE.md", "main", "Bash", command="cat > 'CLAUDE.md' <<EOF\nx\nEOF")
    expect_deny(repo, "2> into .claude", "main", "Bash", command="ls 2> .claude/settings.json")
    expect_deny(repo, "&> into .claude", "main", "Bash", command="ls &> .claude/settings.json")
    expect_deny(repo, "1> into gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command="ls 1> gauntlet/config/x")
    expect_deny(repo, "rm -rf star", "main", "Bash", command="rm -rf *")
    expect_deny(repo, "rm -rf dot", "main", "Bash", command="rm -rf .")
    expect_deny(repo, "rm glob under gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command="rm gauntlet/config/*.txt")
    expect_deny(repo, "cd into gauntlet then write", "main", "Bash", command="cd gauntlet/config && cp /tmp/x crap-allowlist.txt")
    expect_deny(repo, "git -C gauntlet checkout", "main", "Bash", command="git -C gauntlet checkout -- config/checkstyle.xml")
    expect_deny(repo, "write ~/.claude settings", "main", "Write", file_path=os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/settings.json"), content="{}")
    expect_deny(repo, "redirect into ~/.claude", "main", "Bash", command="echo '{\"disableAllHooks\": true}' > ~/.claude/settings.json")
    expect_deny(repo, "checkout -B to base", "main", "Bash", command="git checkout -B claude/feature-x origin/main")
    expect_deny(repo, "switch -C to base", "main", "Bash", command="git switch -C claude/feature-x origin/main")
    expect_deny(repo, "branch -f", "main", "Bash", command="git branch -f claude/feature-x origin/main")
    expect_deny(repo, "branch -D", "main", "Bash", command="git branch -D claude/feature-x")
    expect_allow(repo, "checkout -b new branch", "main", "Bash", command="git checkout -b claude/feature-z")
    expect_allow(repo, "switch existing", "main", "Bash", command="git switch main")
    expect_deny(repo, "gh -R pr merge", "main", "Bash", command="gh -R o/r pr merge 12 --squash")
    expect_deny(repo, "gh --repo pr merge", "main", "Bash", command="gh --repo o/r pr merge 12")
    # --- `gauntlet` as a Gradle task or under build/ is not the kit
    expect_allow(repo, "rm build/gauntlet log with $?", "main", "Bash", command=f"rm -f {M}build/gauntlet/x.log; echo $?")
    expect_allow(repo, "rm missing file then gradlew gauntlet", "main", "Bash",
                 command="rm -f out.log && ./gradlew gauntlet --continue > out.log 2>&1")
    expect_allow(repo, "gradlew gauntlet | tee $VAR", "main", "Bash", command='./gradlew gauntlet --continue 2>&1 | tee "$TMPDIR/run.log"')
    expect_allow(repo, "mkdir $VAR then gradlew gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command='mkdir -p "$SCRATCH" && ./gradlew gauntlet')
    expect_allow(repo, "python -c reads build/gauntlet", "main", "Bash",
                 command=f"python3 -c \"print(open('{M}build/gauntlet/gauntletFast-hook.log').read())\"")
    expect_deny(repo, "rm $VAR with gauntlet assigned", "main", "Bash", command="D=gauntlet; rm -rf $D")
    expect_deny(repo, "rm $VAR next to gradlew gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command="./gradlew gauntlet; X=gauntlet/config; rm -rf $X")
    expect_deny(repo, "echo gauntlet | xargs rm next to gradlew gauntlet", "main", "Bash",
                command="./gradlew gauntlet; echo gauntlet | xargs rm -rf")
    expect_deny(repo, "rm $VAR next to gradlew -p gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command="./gradlew -p gauntlet tasks; rm -rf $X")
    expect_deny(repo, "rm via build/.. back into gauntlet", "main", "Bash", command="rm -rf $P/build/../gauntlet")
    expect_deny(repo, "for ... do rm", "main", "Bash", command='for f in gauntlet/config/*; do rm "$f"; done')
    expect_deny(repo, "then rm", "main", "Bash", command="if true; then rm -rf gauntlet; fi")
    expect_deny(repo, "brace group rm", "main", "Bash", command="{ rm -rf .claude; }")
    expect_deny(repo, "negated rm", "main", "Bash", command="! rm -f CLAUDE.md")
    expect_deny(repo, "do sed -i", "main", "Bash", command="while false; do sed -i 's/8/80/' gauntlet/config/gauntlet.properties; done")
    expect_deny(repo, "then git push --force", "main", "Bash", command="if true; then git push --force; fi")
    expect_deny(repo, "rm via $PWD", "main", "Bash", command="rm -rf $PWD/gauntlet")
    expect_deny(repo, "rm via $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR", "main", "Bash", command='rm -rf "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude"')
    expect_deny(repo, "xargs rm", "main", "Bash", command="git ls-files gauntlet/config | xargs rm -f")
    expect_deny(repo, "sed -i on substitution", "main", "Bash", command="sed -i 's/8/80/' $(git ls-files gauntlet/config/gauntlet.properties)")
    expect_deny(repo, "pushd then sed", "main", "Bash", command="pushd gauntlet/config && sed -i 's/8/80/' gauntlet.properties")

    # --- over-block: the VALUE of an option is not a cluster of flags (`--sort -committerdate` has c, m and d in it;

    for name, command in (

    push = "git push --force origin HEAD"

            ("ksh -c", f"ksh -c '{push}'"),
            ("zsh -ic", f"zsh -ic '{push}'"),

            ("/usr/bin/sudo", f"/usr/bin/sudo {push}"),

            ("substitution after an ANSI-C string", "echo $'it\\'s' \"$(" + push + ")\""),
            ("nested escaped backticks", 'echo "`echo \\`' + push + '\\``"'),
            ("pipe into bash -o pipefail", f"echo '{push}' | bash -o pipefail")):

    for name, command in (

            ("bash -c inside bash -c", "bash -c \"bash -lc 'rm -rf gauntlet'\"")):

    test_java = M + "src/test/java/com/example/service/domain/OrderTest.java"
    expect_deny(repo, "carrier role: reviewer commits through bash -lc", "reviewer", "Bash", command="bash -lc 'git commit -m x'")

            ("push text quoted for another shell's pipe", "echo 'git push --force | bash -o pipefail'"),

            ("the gauntlet task through bash -lc", "bash -lc './gradlew gauntlet'"),

    for name, command in (

    for name, command in (

            ('git status after a nested substitution', 'echo "$(echo "$(echo ")")"; git status)"'),
            ('a harmless case inside a substitution', 'echo "$(case x in x) echo y;; esac)"'),
            ('git log piped into head', "git log --format='%h %s' | head -3"),

    for name, command in (

            ('node with two -e', 'node -e \'console.log(1)\' -e \'require("child_process").execSync("git push --force origin HEAD")\''),
            ('perl -we', 'perl -we \'system("git push --force origin HEAD")\''),
